title: MegaETH Cuts Staff as AI Ambitions Complicate Its Ethereum Scaling Story
summary: Ethereum scaling project MegaETH is reducing its workforce while developing a new artificial-intelligence business, a combination that raises an awkward question for investors and users: what exactly should they expect the project to prioritise? The company has reportedly cut around one-fifth of its...
content:
Ethereum scaling project MegaETH is reducing its workforce while developing a new artificial-intelligence business, a combination that raises an awkward question for investors and users: what exactly should they expect the project to prioritise? The company has reportedly cut around one-fifth of its staff and is directing substantial resources toward an AI marketplace, even as its existing on-chain activity remains under scrutiny.

A strategic pivot is not necessarily a bad decision. Many technology businesses adjust their product mix when customer demand changes. But in crypto, where teams often raise funds on a particular network vision, a change in emphasis deserves careful explanation.

The restructuring is more than a headcount story

The Block reported that MegaETH had reduced staffing by about 20%. Additional reporting described plans to allocate roughly $30 million from treasury resources to an AI-related marketplace scheduled for December. These are plans and reported allocations, not proof that the proposed marketplace is already operating at scale or generating revenue.

The layoff percentage matters, but so does which capabilities remain. An Ethereum scaling network needs engineers working on performance, security, developer tools and operational reliability. If a new AI product draws from the same management attention and treasury, token holders and users need to understand how the two efforts fit together rather than assuming one automatically supports the other.

On-chain traction is the other part of the equation

Reported data placed value locked in the MegaETH ecosystem at about $8.8 million after an earlier period above $240 million. Total value locked can change for many reasons, including token prices, rewards programmes and the movement of a small number of large liquidity providers. It is therefore a useful indicator of deployed capital, but not a complete measure of developer adoption, revenue or user retention.

Even with those caveats, a large decline makes execution questions unavoidable. Are applications attracting repeat users without incentives? Is the underlying network delivering the speed and reliability promised? Can independent developers deploy products that people want to use? Those measures would say more about the scaling thesis than publicity around a new business category.

AI may be complementary, but the link needs proof

There are plausible connections between blockchain infrastructure and AI services, including machine-to-machine settlement, verifiable payments and coordination of agents. NewsBTC's examination of Circle's approach to AI-agent payments illustrates why companies are exploring this intersection. Yet a broad trend is not a commercial plan in itself.

An AI marketplace would need to answer ordinary product questions: who are the customers, what service are they buying, what is the business model and why does this specific blockchain make the experience better? If the answer is primarily that both AI and crypto are fashionable, investors should be sceptical. If the product solves a measurable problem, the new direction could make sense.

Decentralisation promises still need milestones

Reporting has also referenced a planned decentralisation milestone in March 2027. Timelines like that are significant for a scaling network because they speak to who controls upgrades and critical infrastructure. A pivot cannot quietly replace the need to explain governance, operational resilience and user protections.

For Ethereum more broadly, the ecosystem is already navigating difficult market conditions, including the ETF outflows covered in NewsBTC's recent Ether fund report. MegaETH's situation adds a separate company-specific test. The next meaningful update will be evidence of both product execution and the original network commitments, not simply a new roadmap graphic.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: US sellers drive Bitcoin crash, Jensen plots Nvidia comeback: Hodler’s Digest
summary: Anchorage Digital data suggests the Bitcoin selloff is being driven by US investors. A “war room” has been set up by supporters to reinstate Nvidia boss Jensen Huang.
content:
Bitcoin bottomed after the US midterm elections in 2018 and 2022 — and the great Bitcoin crash of November 2026 looks like history repeating. Bitcoin plunged more than $10,000 this week, and is currently trading at $65,116 for a 12.4% loss.

According to Anchorage Digital researcher David Lawant, the call is coming from inside the house. “BTC sell pressure continues to come primarily from the U.S,” he noted, positing a chart highlighting showing continued heavy net taker sell flow primarily on Coinbase compared with overseas exchanges.

The US spot Bitcoin ETFs have seen heavy outflows, losing $2.35 billion over the past two weeks, and influencer Axel Bitblaze noted that Bitcoin fell in the hour before the US open on all but two of the past fifteen days.

Source: Anchorage Digital

Binance founder Changpeng Zhao rebuffed the idea that Binance is behind the crash. “No, Binance did not sell crypto. I bought crypto in the past few days,” he said. He attributed the crash to money shifting to the Anthropic IPO, the Bitcoin ETF outflows, security fears about crypto in general in the wake of the Binance hack, and hot inflation data raising expectations of interest rate hikes. Markets are now pricing in a quarter point Fed hike in December.

Bitcoin fell to a four month low near $62,000 on Sunday but has since rebounded above $65,000. The Crypto Fear and Greed Index fell to 10, which is Extreme Fear.

History provides some good news in that Bitcoin more then doubled in price within 12 months of the 2018 and 2022 midterm elections.

Jensen discusses Nvidia comeback days after resigning

The Financial Times reports that Jensen Huang is plotting a comeback to the top job at Nvidia with allies, following a determined push in Silicon Valley to pressure the board to reinstate him.

Nvidia shares plunged after Huang resigned as CEO and from the board on Nov. 12, with Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress named as interim CEO. The resignation came shortly after news broke he’d had two other affairs, including one with a subordinate.

Multiple people confirmed Huang has been discussing the idea of returning with confidants, even though an independent probe by the board is examining allegations he was romantically involved with a Chinese spy who helped ferry chips to China.

The FT reported one ally saying that supporters have put together a “war room” to reinstate him. “Everybody that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the source said.

A petition to reinstate Huang has garnered more than 100,000 signatures, including 5,600 current Nvidia employees, along with SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

The turmoil at Nvidia has weighed heavily on AI stocks and risk assets like cryptocurrency and the story still has a long way to run, with Congressional moves to investigate the issue and three bills being advanced to tighten AI chip export restrictions to China. According to the New York Time, intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Trump about the allegations Alice Huang was a Chinese spy a year ago, but he did not take any action.

Ethereum should become post-quantum in 2027: Ethlabs

Ethereum research group Ethlabs is withdrawing its Quick Slots proposal from the forthcoming Hegotá upgrade, and has urged core developers to urgently prepare the network for quantum attacks by 2027.

On Wednesday, the group outlined “pqai27,” a proposed roadmap that aims to protect Ethereum against threats from quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

At Devcon, researcher Justin Drake said he hopes to complete the transition in 2028 while the published roadmap still targets December 2029.

Strategy gets booted from MSCI indexes

Index provider MSCI has confirmed Bitcoin treasury company Strategy will be removed from its global equity indexes, following months of debate over whether crypto treasury firms qualify as operating businesses. Japan’s Metaplanet and crypto treasury company Upexi are also marked for deletion, while Ether treasury firm Sharplink is on a watchlist. The changes take effect after market close on Nov. 30.

“Index inclusion meant ordinary passive investors, like someone holding a global index fund in their pension, were getting leveraged Bitcoin exposure they never chose. MSCI just fixed that,” Ryan Kirkley, CEO of Global Settlement Network, told Cointelegraph. Strategy fell 6.49% on Thursday and are down by more than one quarter over the past month.

Bitcoin ETFs shed $2.35B in 2 weeks, BlackRock’s losing streak hits 11

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks, as redemptions reached more than $1 billion each week. 

According to Farside Investors data, spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.07 billion between from Monday to Friday, following $1.28 billion in outflows the previous week, the largest weekly redemptions since late June. 

Friday marked the seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals, with about $1.71 billion redeemed since Nov. 5

Winners and Losers

At the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 12.4% to trade at $65,116, Ethereum (ETH) is down 14.4% to trade at $1,822 and XRP (XRP) is down 13.3% to $0.96. The total market cap is at $2.2 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are Kite (KITE) with a 35.5% gain, Pieverse (PIEVERSE) on 33.8%, and Midnight (CRV) on 28.7%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Zcash (ZEC) which was down 25.4%, Uniswap (UNI) down 23.2% and Aero (AERO) down 23.1%.

Prediction of the Week

Bitcoin’s ‘best buying opportunity ever’ has arrived: Mark Moss

Bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss says that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a new record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” he said.

Top FUD of the Week

Microsoft confirms global outage resolved, rules out cyberattack

Microsoft managed to restore Microsoft 365 services after a massive global outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other applications for more than 24 hours, reiterating that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.

Microsoft said that the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that emerged after a recent network change. “This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI/agents,” the company said.

MegaETH parent cuts 20% of staff amid restructuring, AI push

MEGA, the organization behind Ethereum layer-2 network MegaETH, has reduced its workforce by 20% following months of restructuring as it expands into artificial intelligence products. 

The layoffs come as MEGA shifts its focus toward developing products on the MegaETH network, including artificial intelligence services. The organization has committed $30 million to the initiative.

Metaplanet swings to $170M loss as Bitcoin sale hits earnings

Metaplanet swung to a $170 million net loss in the first nine months of 2026, hit by a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings and a loss on the sale of 10,000 coins to demonstrate its ability to raise cash.

The Japanese company, the world’s second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, posted a net loss of 27.16 billion yen (about $170 million), compared with a profit of 13.53 billion yen ($84.6 million) in the same period last year. A 19.17 billion yen ($119.8 million) loss on the Bitcoin sale and an 8.04 billion yen ($50.3 million) loss from a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings outweighed gains in the operating business.

Top Magazine Features of the Week

Are Alt-L1s over? Security, costs drive smaller chains to Ethereum

L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist.


Paraguay bank collapse shows stablecoins can offer a lifeline... of sorts

Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline.

Should you leave Australia to avoid paying 47% tax on crypto gains?

Some Australian crypto investors are moving overseas to avoid the huge CGT increase from July 2027. But there are also less drastic ways you can pay less tax.

title: Blumenthal Targets CFTC Over Alleged Ties to Kalshi
summary: Blumenthal, who has been active in probing the links between Tether and the Trump administration, said the national commodities regulator might be in the pocket of prediction market platforms, given the ample operating advantages they have gained from recent regulatory actions. Senator Blumenthal Ca...
content:
Blumenthal, who has been active in probing the links between Tether and the Trump administration, said the national commodities regulator might be in the pocket of prediction market platforms, given the ample operating advantages they have gained from recent regulatory actions.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 15, 2026, 5:42 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Senator Blumenthal hinted at probing the CFTC for allegedly favoring prediction platforms like Kalshi.
  • Reports suggest Kalshi pressured the CFTC over delayed approvals for its new crypto perpetual futures.
  • This sparks consumer protection fears and adds to Wall Street’s fight against CFTC stock perpetuals.

Senator Blumenthal Calls for Congress to Take Action Against Prediction Market Platforms

Congress is taking a closer look at the regulatory developments concerning prediction market platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket, and how these could have been favored by federal watchdog action under the Trump Administration.

Senator Richard Blumenthal, a Democrat from Connecticut, is now hinting at a congressional probe into the alleged links between the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) and prediction market platforms after reports indicated that Kalshi was ready to launch perpetual futures even after the regulator greenlit them.

A WSJ article claims that Kalshi had to cancel a gathering at a Brooklyn luxury penthouse when the CFTC did not “move fast enough” to announce that the platform was approved to launch these new perpetual futures. This allegedly prompted a follow-up call from Kalshi CEO Tarek Mansour to CFTC Chairman Michael S. Selig to complain about the situation, with three people with knowledge of the call who spoke on the condition of anonymity to describe a private conversation quoted as sources.

Blumenthal claims this report might be indicative of an unhealthy compromise between the regulator and prediction market companies.

“More strong signs that the CFTC is in prediction market pockets—as it approves sweeping new gambling on stock prices, cryptocurrencies, & more,” Blumenthal stated on social media channels.

“It puts the public in deep peril, setting consumer protection way below industry profits in priority. Time for Congress to act,” Blumenthal concluded, hinting at deeper congressional oversight on this issue.

Blumenthal has probed the crypto industry before, sending letters to Tether to clarify its links to the Trump Administration through a series of millionaire payments made to Nxum, a consulting firm co-founded by Bo Hines, who operated as a digital asset policy advisor for the White House.

These perpetual futures, which allow users to bet on the rise or fall of any cryptocurrency with no expiration date and without exposure to the underlying assets, have become a large part of Kalshi’s activity, registering $5.5 billion in trading two weeks after their May launch.

As the CFTC expands these perpetuals to include U.S. stocks, it is facing opposition from traditional finance exchange giants, which have filed a lawsuit under the Capital Markets Alliance’s (CMA) umbrella alleging that these products must be under the oversight of the Securities and Exchange Commission, as they behave more like security swaps than commodity futures, lacking a fixed expiry date.

About the author

WRITTEN BYSergio Goschenko

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Kava Lend Exploit Exposes a Dangerous Gap in DeFi Collateral Accounting
summary: An exploit at Kava Lend has drained roughly 55 million KAVA tokens from the lending protocol, highlighting a class of DeFi vulnerability that can remain dormant until unusual market conditions make it dangerous. The incident did not involve an attacker magically creating unlimited tokens. Instead,…
content:
An exploit at Kava Lend has drained roughly 55 million KAVA tokens from the lending protocol, highlighting a class of DeFi vulnerability that can remain dormant until unusual market conditions make it dangerous. The incident did not involve an attacker magically creating unlimited tokens. Instead, on-chain analysis indicates that a tiny balance in a largely inactive stablecoin market caused the protocol to overstate the value of collateral, opening the door to repeated borrowing.

The attack and the sharp fall in KAVA's price unfolded on November 14. The protocol team has said the incident was contained within Kava Lend, but a full official post-mortem and recovery plan had not been published in the reporting reviewed for this article.

A nearly empty BUSD market became the weak point

According to The Block's account of the incident, the attacker targeted a Kava Lend market for BUSD, a stablecoin whose issuer stopped minting new tokens in 2023. The market was barely active. By pushing its effective net supply extremely close to zero, the attacker triggered a calculation that exaggerated the accounting value of deposits by approximately 243,000 times.

This was not a huge cash deposit suddenly becoming a huge amount of real money. It was a software-accounting error: the lending system treated collateral as far more valuable than it actually was. Such errors are particularly dangerous in lending protocols because borrowing limits depend on accurate collateral valuations. If that relationship breaks, the system can approve loans that no legitimate market price would support.

Borrowing and bridging made the damage worse

The attacker reportedly executed 127 KAVA borrow transactions, drawing roughly 55.2 million tokens from the pool. At the price before the attack, those tokens were worth approximately $3.76 million. Around 49.2 million KAVA were then sent to BNB Chain through LayerZero, with sales producing about $2.09 million in BNB and USDT, according to the published on-chain analysis.

Those figures describe different things. The larger dollar value is an estimate based on the pre-attack token price, while the smaller amount describes proceeds realised after heavy selling into a falling market. The amount borrowed, value lost by lenders and value ultimately recoverable may differ. A definitive accounting should await the protocol's incident report.

The team's response leaves important questions

Kava said the event was not an infinite-mint problem and was isolated to Kava Lend. It also reported precautionary steps affecting bridging, while some trading venues restricted KAVA transfers. Those actions may limit additional damage, but they do not automatically replenish tokens owed to depositors or explain how the accounting failure escaped detection.

The most useful follow-up is not a dramatic price prediction. It is a clear statement about who bore the loss, whether any market remains impaired, what code changes are proposed and whether those changes have undergone independent review. The availability of an audit label alone cannot substitute for understanding the exact edge case that failed.

DeFi's old accounting problem has not disappeared

Lending protocols routinely make complex decisions using collateral ratios, interest indexes, liquidity pools and oracle prices. As NewsBTC's coverage of Aave governance shows, even mature money markets require ongoing decisions about risk and economic design. Institutional interest in lending infrastructure makes those controls more consequential, not less.

The Kava case is a reminder that the most damaging exploit may come from an apparently forgotten market rather than a heavily traded one. For anyone depositing into a DeFi lender, exposure to every supported collateral market can matter, even if they never personally touch the asset that starts the chain reaction.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Luxor Confirms Bitcoin Mining Hack and Reveals AI-Enabled Attack
summary: Luxor Technology has confirmed an unauthorized redirection of bitcoin mining hashrate through its Commander platform, ending speculation surrounding an alleged attack involving thousands of mining machines. The company says the incident was contained within two hours, and affected customers will rec...
content:
Luxor Technology has confirmed an unauthorized redirection of bitcoin mining hashrate through its Commander platform, ending speculation surrounding an alleged attack involving thousands of mining machines. The company says the incident was contained within two hours, and affected customers will receive full compensation.

Key Takeaways

  • Luxor confirmed that just over a dozen client accounts were affected by unauthorized hashrate redirection through its Commander platform.
  • CEO Nick Hansen attributed the compromise to a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector,” although the company has not publicly detailed the mechanism.
  • Luxor says it patched the vulnerability within two hours, prevented data exfiltration and will compensate affected customers for lost mining revenue.

Luxor Breaks Silence on Bitcoin Mining Security Breach

What initially appeared to be an unverified bitcoin mining hijack has developed into a confirmed security incident, with Luxor Technology acknowledging that attackers redirected mining equipment through its Commander management platform.

In an official statement issued Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, Luxor disclosed that internal monitoring systems detected unauthorized modifications to mining pool configurations, prompting an immediate engineering response. The team wrote:

“Last night our internal monitoring alerted us to an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander. Our on-call engineering team jumped on it right away.”

According to Luxor, just over a dozen customer accounts were affected, with mining machines temporarily redirected to another pool. The company maintains that no information was stolen from its systems.

“Impact: just over a dozen client accounts. Affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window. No data was leaked or exfiltrated from our systems,” the team disclosed on X.

Luxor explained that its engineers patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected equipment to its original configurations. The company also committed to reimbursing every affected customer for the computational power diverted during the incident. “Compensation: every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if it had mined normally,” Luxor added.

The company further emphasized that the compromise was confined to Commander, with its mining pool and LuxOS firmware remaining unaffected.

CEO Nick Hansen Attributes Compromise to Sophisticated AI-Enabled Attack

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen subsequently offered a more personal account of the incident, acknowledging the operational disruption and identifying what he described as an artificial intelligence-assisted intrusion.

“The last 12 hours have been pretty rough,” Hansen wrote. He said the compromise began around 6 p.m. Pacific time Saturday, Nov. 14, affecting a subset of Commander customers. The CEO continued:

“Around 6:00p PDT yesterday, a subset of Commander customers were compromised, through a sophisticated AI-enabled vector.”

Although Hansen attributed the intrusion to an AI-enabled method, Luxor has not yet published technical findings establishing precisely how the attackers gained access or manipulated mining configurations.

Hansen detailed that engineers identified and patched the issue before undertaking the more laborious process of restoring affected machines. He also apologized to customers and reiterated that Luxor would cover their losses. He said:

“I apologize. You trust us with your fleet, and we need to be better.”

The executive also remarked that affected customers would receive additional information by email, while Luxor promised a comprehensive post-mortem examining the incident.

OCEAN Mining Data Reveals Unusual Hashrate Activity

Before Luxor’s confirmation, reports circulating late Saturday suggested approximately 64,000 mining machines, representing an estimated 13 exahash per second (EH/s), had been redirected toward the Ocean mining pool. Those figures remain independently unverified, and Luxor’s disclosure of just over a dozen compromised accounts does not establish the total number of affected machines.

Ocean, a noncustodial Bitcoin mining pool launched in 2023 with financial backing from Jack Dorsey, allows miners to receive payments directly through block coinbase transactions. Its public dashboard showed unusual mining activity around the reported incident, while a suspected destination address accumulated an estimated 0.65761026 BTC in mining rewards.

Mempool.space developer Mononaut observed:

“Oof, about 0.657 BTC of shares earned from stolen hash, per ocean’s dashboard”

However, estimated rewards do not constitute completed payments. Available blockchain records showed no confirmed incoming transactions to the suspected address, suggesting the operator had not collected bitcoin from the redirected mining activity.

CoreX Hosting, which initially publicized the suspected attack, subsequently reported that the unauthorized hashrate had declined to approximately 100 petahash per second (PH/s).

Luxor’s confirmation resolves the central question of whether unauthorized redirection occurred, but important details remain unsettled. The precise number of affected machines, total computational power diverted, and technical mechanics of the alleged AI-assisted compromise await further disclosure.

For mining operators, the incident illustrates how unauthorized changes to fleet configurations can jeopardize revenue without requiring attackers to seize cryptocurrency directly. Luxor’s compensation pledge addresses the immediate financial consequences, but its forthcoming investigation will face a more consequential question: how attackers obtained sufficient control to redirect industrial mining equipment in the first place.

title: Ether ETFs Approach an Unwanted Record After Seven Weeks of Outflows
summary: US spot Ether exchange-traded funds are edging toward an uncomfortable milestone. The category has now recorded seven consecutive weeks of net withdrawals, placing it one additional negative week away from matching the longest losing streak identified in the current dataset. That is an especially aw...
content:
US spot Ether exchange-traded funds are edging toward an uncomfortable milestone. The category has now recorded seven consecutive weeks of net withdrawals, placing it one additional negative week away from matching the longest losing streak identified in the current dataset. That is an especially awkward backdrop for Ethereum supporters who see exchange-traded products as a bridge between the network and traditional investment accounts.

The withdrawal trend does not tell us that institutions have abandoned Ethereum, nor does it measure how much activity is occurring on the blockchain. It does indicate that ETF demand has been persistently soft during a period of broader market stress.

The numbers show a sustained retreat

The Block's review of SoSoValue figures put net withdrawals from US spot Ether ETFs at about $398.9 million for the week ending November 13. That marked a seventh consecutive weekly outflow, with cumulative withdrawals of roughly $2.42 billion since late September. Another negative week would tie the eight-week losing streaks the category has previously experienced.

A single week's figure can be influenced by a handful of large transactions, but seven weeks is long enough to warrant closer examination. NewsBTC's report on the November 9 Ether ETF outflow captured one daily episode; the accumulated weekly data reveals how the pressure has persisted beyond that session.

Why ETF sentiment may diverge from Ethereum usage

Owning an Ether ETF share and using Ethereum are fundamentally different activities. A fund investor primarily seeks financial exposure to ETH's price, subject to the product's particular structure and fees. A blockchain user might be paying transaction charges, supplying liquidity, issuing a token or building an application. The two can influence one another over time, but neither provides a complete picture of the other.

For this reason, it would be a mistake to use fund outflows as evidence that smart contracts are no longer being used. A better test of network health also considers transactions, fees, applications, security and adoption. Those indicators require interpretation too, particularly as activity shifts across Ethereum's scaling ecosystem.

Bitcoin's ETF weakness is part of the same backdrop

The Ether figures arrived in a week when spot Bitcoin ETFs also lost more than $1 billion, and other crypto fund categories largely experienced withdrawals. That broad pattern suggests investors may be reducing digital-asset exposure generally rather than rotating decisively from ETH into BTC. It is a different story from one in which capital leaves one token product but pours into another.

There is still an important distinction between price losses and fund flows. ETH's falling market value can reduce ETF assets without any redemption, while net withdrawals reflect investor activity through the fund structure. Keeping those measures separate prevents the discussion from exaggerating the selling actually revealed by the data.

Ethereum's longer-term thesis faces a shorter-term test

The network's DeFi ecosystem continues to evolve, including proposals over how protocols capture fees and share economic value. Aave's recent reserve-factor discussion is one example of the operational debates taking place independently of fund investor sentiment.

For the next trading week, investors will watch whether Ether funds can interrupt the run of negative flows and whether the change is broad or concentrated in one vehicle. A positive week would not erase the preceding losses, but it would be a measurable sign that some buyers are reconsidering. Until then, the ETF channel remains an obvious pressure point for Ethereum's market narrative.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

title: Coinone Data Breach Exposes Passwords and Sensitive Customer Records
summary: South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Coinone disclosed a significant customer data breach on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, after attackers infiltrated its outsourced support provider, MetaM, potentially exposing passwords, banking information, national identification numbers, and cryptocurrency wallet deta...
content:
South Korean cryptocurrency exchange Coinone disclosed a significant customer data breach on Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026, after attackers infiltrated its outsourced support provider, MetaM, potentially exposing passwords, banking information, national identification numbers, and cryptocurrency wallet details belonging to customers.

Key Takeaways

  • Coinone’s outsourced customer support provider, MetaM, suffered an intrusion involving 11 categories of potentially sensitive customer information.
  • The exchange maintains that its trading infrastructure and cryptocurrency wallets remain uncompromised, although the number of affected customers remains unknown.
  • The incident adds to a growing collection of cryptocurrency industry data breaches in 2026, raising questions about third-party security and customer privacy.

Coinone Data Breach Exposes 11 Categories of Sensitive Information

According to Coinone’s official disclosure, the intrusion occurred around 4 a.m. Korean Standard Time on Thursday, Nov. 12, when an unauthorized attacker accessed servers operated by MetaM, which handles the exchange’s telephone and online customer consultations. The contractor notified Coinone at approximately 9:20 a.m. that morning, while the exchange publicly disclosed the incident on Nov. 15.

Coinone ranks as South Korea’s third-largest cryptocurrency exchange by trading activity, trailing Bithumb in second place and market leader Upbit. The South Korean trading platform counts OKX among its financial backers, with the exchange holding a 20% stake and the remaining ownership divided among Coinone founder and CEO Cha Myung-hoon, Com2uS Holdings, and Korea Investment & Securities.

In its announcement on Sunday, Coinone acknowledged the seriousness of the security failure, stating:

“Although we have made protecting your personal information our top priority, we must inform you that an external attacker gained unauthorized access to the servers of a contractor we hired to handle customer support, and your personal information was leaked.”

The exchange added:

“As the company that outsourced this work, we feel a deep sense of responsibility for this incident and sincerely apologize.”

The potentially compromised know your customer (KYC) information encompasses 11 categories: telephone numbers, names, email addresses, dates of birth, bank account numbers, passwords, resident registration numbers, identification document issuance dates, residential addresses, cryptocurrency wallet addresses, and transaction identifiers (TXIDs).

Not every customer necessarily had all 11 categories exposed. The compromised records concern information voluntarily supplied during previous customer support interactions, meaning customers who never contacted Coinone’s support center fall outside the incident’s identified scope.

Coinone has not disclosed how many individuals were affected or precisely how much information attackers obtained. The company intends to introduce a dedicated lookup service allowing customers to determine which personal details were involved.

Coinone Insists Customer Funds Are Safe Despite Security Breach

Despite the sensitive nature of the exposed records, Coinone maintains that its principal trading infrastructure remained untouched. Its customer accounts, transaction systems and cryptocurrency wallets operate independently of MetaM’s compromised servers.

The exchange emphasized:

“The partial information leaked so far is not sufficient for a third party to log in to your account or withdraw your assets.”

Coinone explained that its authentication procedures require additional verification through registered one-time passwords or Kakaotalk, while unauthorized login methods are blocked. Nevertheless, the absence of a direct wallet compromise does not eliminate the possibility of subsequent financial fraud.

Following the discovery, Coinone said it blocked suspicious IP addresses, restricted access to compromised systems, strengthened transaction monitoring and temporarily transferred outsourced customer support operations to email-only service.

The exchange also notified the Korea Internet & Security Agency, Personal Information Protection Commission, and Financial Supervisory Service. Investigators, Coinone explained, are examining the intrusion alongside MetaM and outside security specialists.

Particularly concerning is the potential misuse of customer support conversations. Attackers possessing identification numbers, banking information, and historical correspondence could construct convincing impersonation and phishing schemes targeting unsuspecting customers.

Coinone cautioned:

“Calls or messages that reference your past support conversations may also be impersonation attempts, so please be cautious.”

Customers who previously disclosed passwords during support interactions were instructed to change those credentials immediately, including on unrelated services where identical passwords were reused.

Five Major Crypto Data Breaches Cast Shadow Over 2026

Coinone’s disclosure follows several other notable customer information breaches involving cryptocurrency businesses during 2026, illustrating how attackers increasingly exploit operational systems beyond traditional exchange wallets.

On Nov. 3, Gnosis Pay experienced unauthorized access involving its legacy cryptocurrency debit card infrastructure, potentially exposing customer information, including payment card details and wallet addresses.

Chainalysis disclosed a separate security incident in late October, subsequently expanding its findings in early November. The analytics company’s investigation identified exposed account credentials, password hashes and authentication tokens, although it reported no evidence that sensitive investigation records were accessed.

South Korean exchange Bithumb also encountered unauthorized access to internal communications infrastructure in October. Its investigation identified records associated with 6,444 customers, including directly exposed personal information belonging to 844 individuals.

Meanwhile, Coinbase disclosed customer information exposure associated with a September security incident involving third-party analytics provider Amplitude. The exchange maintained that its own infrastructure and customer funds were unaffected.

These incidents differ considerably in scope and technical circumstances, but collectively demonstrate that customer information can remain vulnerable even when cryptocurrency custody systems escape compromise. Under South Korean privacy legislation, affected Coinone customers may pursue statutory damages of up to 3 million won when proving actual financial losses is difficult.

For Coinone, the unresolved questions concern the number of affected customers, the information actually extracted, and whether additional fraud emerges. The broader concern extends beyond cryptocurrency theft: Even exchanges that successfully protect customer assets can expose users to lasting financial and identity risks through inadequately secured third-party relationships.

title: Stablecoin Supply Shrinkage Raises a Bigger Question About Crypto Liquidity
summary: Crypto investors spend plenty of time staring at Bitcoin charts, but one of the more revealing signals this month may be the amount of dollar-backed stablecoins circulating across the market. Recent data suggests that the combined supply of major stablecoins has contracted materially from its earlie...
content:
Crypto investors spend plenty of time staring at Bitcoin charts, but one of the more revealing signals this month may be the amount of dollar-backed stablecoins circulating across the market. Recent data suggests that the combined supply of major stablecoins has contracted materially from its earlier peak. That matters because these tokens are often the cash-like instruments traders use to move money between exchanges, DeFi protocols and new positions.

A shrinking supply does not automatically cause a market crash, and it certainly does not mean every stablecoin holder has left crypto. It does, however, raise a practical question: is the industry's readily deployable dollar liquidity getting smaller just as prices are falling?

The size of the decline is difficult to ignore

CoinDesk's November 15 market report described the combined stablecoin market retreating toward roughly $244 billion, compared with a peak near $270 billion in May 2026. It also cited Glassnode data indicating a decline of approximately $17 billion over a one-month period. These are market snapshots from particular datasets, not a count of dollars sitting in every crypto trading account.

The distinction is significant. Stablecoin supply changes when issuers create or redeem tokens, but balances also shift among blockchains, venues and use cases. An on-chain transfer from one exchange to another does not shrink total issuance. A redemption in which tokens are destroyed can do so. Comparing data providers therefore requires consistent definitions and time windows.

Why traders care about stablecoin balances

Stablecoins serve several functions at once. They can be a temporary refuge during volatile markets, a settlement instrument for trading and a payments rail for companies that want digital dollars without holding Bitcoin or Ether. When aggregate supply grows, traders often interpret that as potential purchasing power entering the ecosystem. When it contracts, one plausible reading is that capital is being withdrawn or used elsewhere.

But supply and demand are not a one-step equation. A dollar token sitting idle in a wallet may be less important to near-term prices than a smaller amount actively circulating through exchanges. Conversely, a market can recover even while headline supply remains flat if existing balances change hands more frequently. The connection is useful, not deterministic.

Payments activity can tell a different story

The business case for stablecoins does not disappear when trading demand weakens. NewsBTC's coverage of Bitso Business's reported payment volumes illustrates how companies use digital dollars for transfers and settlement rather than speculation. Likewise, USDC's rollout through Samsung Wallet on Solana shows the payments and consumer-access dimension.

That creates an interesting tension. Trading-led demand can ebb even as infrastructure for real-world payments develops. Analysts should therefore ask where supply is shrinking, what users are doing with the remaining balances and whether dollar liquidity on exchanges is tightening faster than demand in payments networks.

What to watch as the market tries to stabilise

Net issuance and redemptions from major issuers are an obvious starting point. Exchange stablecoin balances, cross-chain transfers and DeFi borrowing rates can help provide context, provided their methodology is clear. More importantly, these series should be compared with spot buying and ETF flows rather than used in isolation.

A return to stablecoin growth would not guarantee a rally, but it could indicate that more cash-like capacity is entering the system. Until then, the contraction is another reminder that crypto prices are shaped by the availability of capital as much as by the promise of the underlying technology.

Written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.

Published:Nov 15, 2026, 2:15 PM EST

Lee, Chairman of Bitmine and CIO of Fundstrat Capital, stressed that while bitcoin and ether have been selling off over the past week, he remains bullish on the market’s future, citing several factors that point to a supercycle bigger than past cycles.

WRITTEN BY

SHARE

Published: Nov 15, 2026, 2:15 PM EST

Key Takeaways

  • Tom Lee dismissed the crypto downturn, arguing that strong tradfi adoption will drive a new supercycle.
  • He linked the weakness to temporary shocks, including the Nvidia selloff, AI security fears, and IPOs.
  • Lee expects digital assets to become the settlement layer for traditional finance as tokenization grows.

Fundstrat’s Tom Lee Talks Crypto Supercycle, Says Market Weakness Is Temporary

Tom Lee, Chairman of Ethereum-aligned Bitmine and CIO of Fundstrat Capital, has dismissed the current low sentiment in the crypto market, stressing that fundamentals remain strong and anticipating a new positive cycle for the crypto ecosystem.

On social media, Lee acknowledged that crypto has been under intense selling pressure, with bitcoin reaching near $62K levels and ether nearing $1.7K. Nonetheless, he highlights that the price action shows a disconnect with fundamentals, which have been positive, as many banks have been announcing the use of crypto and blockchain, with tokenization becoming a trend.

For Lee, the current market weakness is caused by temporary factors that, put together, have caused a decoupling of the crypto market from the wider stock market, which has still managed to maintain positive numbers in 2026 despite being hit by the Nvidia downturn and the expectation of more rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

Lee pinpointed several causes for this downturn, including the selloff caused by the situation that Nvidia experienced last week, affecting Asian retail markets; the upcoming Anthropic initial public offering, which is expected to siphon capital from other risk options; the movements of investors who recently received funds from Binance’s $6.3 billion hack from speculative crypto holdings to cash and stablecoins; and the upcoming scrutiny of the chip industry following the resignation of NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang.

At a deeper level, Lee recognizes that the recent string of security incidents affecting leading cryptocurrency institutions has awakened concerns about AI’s rise and how threat actors using these tools can break into anything. This creates existential fears in some investors, who may prefer to steer clear of assets linked to digital and tech systems, including cryptocurrency.

Cobra, owner and maintainer of the bitcoin.org website, recently touched on this specific issue, stressing that threat actors with easy access to AI tools have made bitcoin self-custody “extremely risky.”

Even so, Lee remains bullish about the relevance of crypto for the future of financial markets, with digital assets becoming the settlement layer for transactions as tradfi pivots to these tools. According to Lee, this transformation of capital markets will bring a new period of prosperity for the crypto market, producing a so-called “supercycle” for the asset class, predicted to be bigger than other so-called supercycles.

Lee has been consistent with his positive remarks, earning his reputation as a permabull. In May, he highlighted that Bitmine remained optimistic about ether’s surge, mentioning Wall Street tokenization and agentic AI as long-term drivers of this supercycle.

Sergio is a cryptocurrency journalist based in Venezuela with 2,000+ articles published, cited in dozens of papers and reports.

title: Strategist Sees Bitcoin Path to $170K Despite Selloff, Says ‘Buy the Fear’
summary: Bitcoin could recover toward $170,000 in 2027 under a scenario outlined by Wellington-Altus strategist James Thorne after the selloff. He attributed the decline to leverage while identifying price levels that would support or invalidate his outlook. Thorne Outlines a Route to New Bitcoin Highs James...
content:
Bitcoin could recover toward $170,000 in 2027 under a scenario outlined by Wellington-Altus strategist James Thorne after the selloff. He attributed the decline to leverage while identifying price levels that would support or invalidate his outlook.

Key Takeaways

  • Thorne targeted $117,000 by mid-2027 before a possible record high.
  • Bitcoin must reclaim $73,000, then clear $87,000 in his scenario.
  • A decline below $57,000 would invalidate the strategist’s outlook.

Thorne Outlines a Route to New Bitcoin Highs

James Thorne, chief market strategist at Canadian wealth management firm Wellington-Altus, outlined on Nov. 14 a potential bitcoin recovery toward $150,000-$170,000 by the end of 2027. He questioned whether the selloff had established a bottom and whether a new record could follow next year. His case combined a developing chart pattern with his assessment that leverage drove the decline.

In his bitcoin forecast shared on X, Thorne set out the sequence of price levels needed for that recovery. He stated:

“Reclaim $73k. Confirm above $87k. Target $117k by mid-2027, then a break of the $126k high and $150–170k by year-end. That’s what the chart says.”

The inverse head-and-shoulders formation he described consists of three successive lows, with the middle one deepest, and can signal a reversal of a downtrend. He placed the left shoulder, or first low, near $59,000 and the head, or central low, around $57,000. The right shoulder, a third low above the head, was still forming in his assessment.

The $87,000 Threshold Behind the Forecast

A neckline connects the rebound highs between those lows, marking resistance where selling previously stalled price advances. Thorne’s chart placed that zone around $82,000-$87,000, with confirmation requiring bitcoin to rise above its upper boundary. Fidelity’s explanation of inverse head-and-shoulders formations identifies an upward neckline breakout as the pattern’s completion.

Subsequent trading pushed bitcoin below $62,000 on Nov. 15, with Coinglass recording a low of $61,956.30. That moved the price closer to Thorne’s $57,000 invalidation level while leaving it below his initial $73,000 recovery threshold. He stated: “Below $57k, I’m wrong.”

Such targets draw on historical prices and chart structure. Technical and fundamental analysis examine different evidence, with fundamentals encompassing economic conditions and adoption. A completed price pattern would support the technical interpretation; evidence about demand and liquidity would bear on the broader market assessment.

Liquidation Losses Accompany Pressure on Demand

Coinglass figures published on Nov. 13 showed crypto liquidations totaling $1.62 billion over 24 hours, including $1.46 billion in bullish positions. Those losses documented substantial forced closures during the decline. Thorne offered his interpretation:

“This washout was leverage, not fundamentals. Buy the fear.”

Glassnode’s Nov. 11 assessment nevertheless identified shrinking liquidity and weaker U.S. demand. Its findings included a $14.2 billion contraction in stablecoin supply over 30 days and $1.6 billion in net withdrawals from U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs across 20 trading sessions. Bitcoin also traded at a discount on Coinbase, reinforcing the firm’s assessment of weak U.S. buying interest alongside the derivatives unwind.

By Nov. 14, reduced leverage and renewed whale accumulation offered potential recovery signals amid those pressures. Whale accumulation refers to rising balances in wallets holding large amounts of bitcoin. Glassnode identified accumulation among wallets holding 100 to 10,000 BTC. Smaller holders and certain larger cohorts continued reducing their balances.

summary:

content:

Sunday, 15/11/2026 | 17:24 GMT by Arnab Shome

  • According to Calcalist, layoffs at eToro may occur in the coming weeks.
  • The fintech cut 7 per cent of its workforce, or about 105 employees, last January.

eToro (NASDAQ: ETOR) is planning a second round of layoffs in the coming weeks that could affect dozens of employees globally, Israeli media outlet Calcalist reported. The US-listed company laid off 7 per cent of its workforce, or around 105 employees, last January.

Finance Magnates approached eToro to confirm the upcoming layoffs but had not received a response as of press time.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Second Round of Layoffs in 12 Months

According to eToro's IPO prospectus, it had 1,501 employees across more than 10 offices globally and working remotely by the end of 2024.

eToro is headquartered in Israel and has offices in the UK, Cyprus, Belgium, Germany, Denmark, the United States, Australia, Abu Dhabi, Singapore, Seychelles, Malta, and Gibraltar.

During the January layoffs, which Finance Magnates reported exclusively, eToro’s co-founder and CEO, Yoni Assia, said the move was meant to “align our resources with our key priorities and leverage process automation and AI to operate more efficiently and focus on the areas most critical to our long-term success.”

Interestingly, the fintech recently reported a sharp drop in its revenue and net income for the third quarter of 2026, which was primarily driven by declining demand for cryptocurrency trading. Its clients placed 2 million crypto trades in October, 62% fewer than a year earlier.

Its net income fell 74 per cent year-over-year to $15 million, while net contribution declined 13 per cent to $186 million.

The Struggling ETOR Shares

Founded in 2007, eToro went public in May last year at a valuation of about $4.4 billion. The number was significantly lower than the $10.4 billion it had targeted in a failed SPAC merger in 2021. It raised $250 million at a $3.5 billion valuation in March 2023.

Despite its bumper IPO, with around a 40 per cent listing uptick, eToro shares dropped by about 65 per cent, hitting a 52-week low this week. ETOR shares closed at $22.5 on Friday.

Meanwhile, Assia also said during a recent analyst call that the fintech wants to generate $100 million in revenue in Latin America within two to three years. The base will be LB Finanzas, an Argentine investing and payments app that the company agreed to buy for less than $20 million.

title: ChatGPT Wallet vs. Google Gemini: Who Will Lead AI Shopping and Personal Finance?
summary: OpenAI and Google are pushing artificial intelligence deeper into everyday money decisions, but their latest wallet features target two distinct parts of the consumer experience.
content:
Skip to content

OpenAI and Google are pushing artificial intelligence deeper into everyday money decisions, but their latest wallet features target two distinct parts of the consumer experience.

ChatGPT Wallet enables AI agents to complete online purchases with user approval, while Google Gemini uses financial transaction data to deliver personalized spending insights, subscription tracking, and budgeting assistance. Both announcements, made on November 13, 2026, highlight how AI platforms are expanding beyond traditional conversations.

ChatGPT Wallet Brings AI Agents Into Online Shopping

OpenAI has introduced ChatGPT Wallet, a payment feature that allows its always-on AI agents, known as dots, to complete online purchases on behalf of users. The feature is designed to move AI beyond product research and recommendations by allowing agents to handle checkout through supported websites.

OpenAI’s new feature enables its always-on AI agents, Dots, to complete online purchases securely with explicit user approval for every transaction. Source: ChatGPT via X

The payment process retains user control. Customers first add an eligible payment card to their wallet. When an agent finds a product, users can review the selected items, purchase total, and payment method before approving the transaction through a security check such as Face ID or fingerprint authentication.

Security is central to the system. OpenAI has partnered with American Express, Mastercard, and Visa to use tokenized payments instead of exposing actual card details. Following approval, the payment network generates a temporary substitute containing the information needed to complete the transaction.

This approach prevents the AI agent and merchant from accessing the user’s actual card details. OpenAI also says eligible purchases retain existing card rewards and protections for qualifying disputes.

Mastercard Executive Vice President Sherri Haymond described the objective, saying, “An agent making a purchase should strengthen, not bypass, the trust built into payments.”

ChatGPT Wallet began rolling out on November 13 to US-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older with eligible US-issued cards. OpenAI is initially limiting access while it evaluates real-world transactions and works with businesses, banks, and payment providers to improve compatibility.

Google Gemini Adds AI-Powered Personal Finance Insights

Google is approaching AI-powered financial services from a different direction. Its new Google Wallet integration connects spending information to Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature, allowing the assistant to provide financial guidance based on users’ transaction histories.

Google’s integration of Wallet into Gemini’s Personal Intelligence feature enables AI-driven financial insights using users’ spending data directly within the app. Source: Google via X

US users can connect Google Wallet to Gemini and ask questions about their spending habits by tagging @Google Wallet in conversations. The assistant can generate dynamic charts showing cash flow, asset allocation, and budgets directly within the chat.

Subscription tracking is another feature. Gemini can identify recurring payments across linked accounts and highlight subscriptions whose prices have increased. Users can also review previous spending on categories such as gifts and travel to develop personalized holiday budgets.

Google demonstrated how the feature could support savings planning through a sample request to save $1,000 over three months. Gemini can analyze spending patterns and suggest adjustments, such as reducing dining, rideshare, and subscription expenses.

The integration also supports Plaid, allowing users to connect eligible bank accounts and credit cards to Google Wallet for deeper financial analysis.

Unlike ChatGPT Wallet, however, Google’s feature does not authorize AI-driven purchases or financial transactions. Google emphasizes that Gemini has read-only access to connected account information. As the company explained, the assistant cannot “move, manage, or invest your money.”

Users can also enable or disable the connection through Personal Intelligence settings.

ChatGPT Wallet vs. Google Gemini: Security and Privacy Differences

Both companies are placing user authorization at the center of their financial AI strategies, but their security models serve different purposes.

ChatGPT Wallet focuses on protecting payment credentials during agent-led purchases. Tokenization keeps actual card information away from AI agents and merchants, while biometric approval provides an additional authorization step before checkout.

OpenAI and Google are expanding AI-powered financial services, enabling ChatGPT to facilitate purchases and Gemini to analyze spending and track subscriptions. Source: @ANCrypto_/X

Google Gemini prioritizes controlled access to financial information. Its integration allows the assistant to analyze transaction data without gaining permission to transfer funds or manage investments. Connecting accounts through Plaid is optional, and users retain control over the connection.

The distinction is important. OpenAI is developing a system that can initiate and complete commercial transactions after approval, whereas Google is building an AI assistant that interprets financial activity and helps users make informed decisions.

Both approaches still depend on consumer trust. Payment security, data privacy, accurate recommendations, and transparent authorization will influence how widely people adopt these financial tools.

Who Will Lead AI Shopping and Personal Finance?

The latest developments do not establish a direct winner because ChatGPT Wallet and Google Gemini currently address different needs.

OpenAI has an early advantage in AI shopping by connecting product discovery with payment execution. Its partnerships with established card networks provide an existing payment infrastructure, although merchant compatibility and the limited initial rollout could affect adoption.

Google, meanwhile, is focusing on personalized financial insights. Its integration with Google Wallet and Plaid gives Gemini access to spending information that can support budgeting, subscription monitoring, and savings planning. Its read-only approach also establishes a clear boundary around financial transactions.

Availability is another difference. ChatGPT Wallet initially targets eligible US ChatGPT Pro subscribers, while Google’s Google Wallet integration is rolling out to Gemini app users in the United States across web and mobile.

Ultimately, the two developments represent different directions in the expansion of AI-powered financial services. OpenAI is moving toward agent-led commerce, while Google is strengthening AI-assisted personal finance management.

Their long-term adoption will depend on how reliably these features work, whether users trust AI with sensitive financial information, and how quickly access expands beyond their initial US markets.

title: Enterprise blockchain is going to come back from the dead
summary: With scalability, privacy tools and onchain liquidity improving, businesses may finally have the infrastructure to make enterprise blockchain work.
content:
Opinion by Paul Brody, founder and chief executive, Nightfall Networks

Do you remember Pets.com? It raised $110 million from Amazon and others to build a business where people ordered pet toys and dog food online.

The company crashed and burned, and everyone learned an important lesson: you can’t profitably ship a 50-pound bag of dog food to a customer’s door.

As online retail entrepreneur Ed Baum asked in a 2001 postmortem: “Did Pets.com’s business plan assume the invention of transporters to magically move bags of pet food without shipping costs?”

Please, whatever you do, don’t share this with the people at Chewy; they might not realize their business model doesn’t work. Chewy reported $12.6 billion in sales and $223 million in net income in its latest fiscal year.

The real lesson of Pets.com wasn’t that shipping dog food was a bad idea. It’s that the idea arrived before the logistics, customer habits and unit economics required to make it work.

As it was with chew toys and dog food, so it may be with enterprise blockchains.

Collectively, the crypto industry probably incinerated just as much money trying that between 2017 and 2023 as Pets.com. Maybe more. But the dozens of companies that went after enterprise blockchain were not delusional; they were just too early.

Why businesses need enterprise blockchains

It’s not hard to understand the appeal of enterprise blockchain solutions, at least superficially. Nearly all enterprise systems today tend to fail at the boundaries between companies. There are two failure modes: mode 1, the OG failure mode, where collaboration information is constantly out of sync.

In this world, enterprise IT systems are islands, communicating asynchronously with each other by digital text messages and emailed spreadsheets. It’s cheap and easy to set up, if you don’t mind always having slightly wrong information.

Related: Privacy is missing ingredient for business blockchain adoption: EY exec

Failure mode two is the costly, real-time proprietary integration. Powerful industry leaders politely request their key suppliers and partners to join their closed but always-on networks.

Chewy reported $223 million in net income in its latest fiscal year. Source: Chewy.

These are very costly, but they work well and leave everyone with a kind of business version of Stockholm syndrome, where you come to appreciate the thoroughness and efficiency of the digital choke-hold you are in.

Blockchains offered a better path forward: shared information and business logic across an open ecosystem. All the benefits of a proprietary system in terms of real-time visibility and efficiency, without the lock-in.

Sometime around 2017, this started to look like a very obvious good idea. Investment poured in, consortia launched, press releases were drafted and released, and then pretty much everything crashed and burned. TradeLens, We.Trade, Contour, B3i, ASX Chess, Everledger. All came and went in just a few years.

Though there is a lot of nuance to the details of each of these stories, they all largely have one thing in common: they had to do unnatural things to make up for the lack of privacy available natively in blockchains.

Companies need privacy, not transparency

No company wants their competition to see what they’re doing in detail. Mostly, this meant building a private/permissioned chain and then doing lots of non-blockchain-like things to it and in it to try to keep information private. The results were uniformly slow and expensive and failed to gain traction.

It’s hard to understate the bloodbath of companies and startups that tried and failed to make enterprise blockchain work. A quick web and history search turned up 18 different ones, some of them well-known.

Many had big-name backers, from major banks like Deutsche Bank and HSBC to technology companies like IBM. Pedigreed parents and big brands made no difference — privacy didn’t work and the results were dismal.

What few survivors of this are left have “de-chained” themselves — giving up the blockchain theater and reverting to a classic software-as-a-service (SaaS) model. Many companies that tried and tested these permissioned enterprise systems as users came away from their experience with a clear learning: we tried blockchain, it didn’t work.

That’s unfortunate because everything is different now.

Blockchains today have scalability, privacy and liquidity

Blockchains have scale. Ethereum in 2020 handled 1 million transactions a day and costs per transaction periodically spiked to $30-50 when demand was high. Today, most transactions get done under a penny and capacity is ramping toward billions of transactions a day. Nobody talks about the “trilemma” anymore. Ethereum is decentralized and it is scaled.

Related: Ethereum’s Glamsterdam upgrade launches on Sepolia testnet

Privacy is different now, too. While privacy is still not the default setting, a huge range of privacy tools and systems are now available, from privacy pools to zero-knowledge roll-ups and full privacy chains.

On top of that, Ethereum is building a range of tools that will add basic elements of privacy at multiple levels in the network. The result: it’s now possible to run business operations at scale with a high degree of privacy.

Finally, there’s the money. It’s all moving onchain. Regulators around the globe have blessed stablecoins and the result is a tsunami of liquidity, with transaction volume reaching almost $1.8 trillion in June.

If we combine the operational benefits of blockchains with the financial ones, we get something that enterprises have never really had before: a single ecosystem where you can not only buy, sell, and move assets, but get paid for them as well.

There was just under $1.8 trillion in adjusted stablecoin transaction volume in June. Source: Visa

The return on investment from every single component of this equation is big. Combined, they can yield colossal advantages. McKinsey partners even found that digital supply chain tools could make inventory reductions of 35-75% possible through better planning.

More conservatively, from my experience in the field, just switching away from the existing cascades of spreadsheets and electronic data interchange (EDI) messages can allow firms to run most supply chains with about 20% less inventory at the same service level. That’s worth billions in working capital in most industries.

It gets better from there. Smart contracts reduce the time required to handle many business contract rules from days to minutes and cut the costs of administration in half.

Microsoft began moving its Xbox video game network onto smart contracts for handling royalties and cut the time to access monthly royalty statements from 45 days to four minutes. All that while handling more than 2 million transactions a day.

And once you have inventories, contracts, purchase orders and invoices onchain, you can go after working capital directly as well.

When you can prove your purchase order originates from a top-quality buyer, you can access credit for less. And when you have full visibility into inventory and delivery status, you can factor receivables immediately and efficiently.

The possibilities and the returns are big. The use cases are obvious. It’s time to try again.

Magazine: What Democrats’ US midterm sweep means for the CLARITY Act

About the author: Paul Brody is the Founder and CEO of Nightfall Networks, a blockchain technology company focused on building robust privacy systems for enterprise users. He is the former Global Blockchain Leader at EY and the former Chairman of the Enterprise Ethereum Alliance.

title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Today: $65K Support Under Pressure as Glassnode Maps $60K–$62K Liquidation Cluster
summary: Bitcoin faces renewed selling pressure near $65,000 as weakening demand, negative ETF flows, and underwater investor positions increase downside risks.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Bitcoin faces renewed selling pressure near $65,000 as weakening demand, negative ETF flows, and underwater investor positions increase downside risks.

Glassnode’s futures liquidation heat map identifies a concentrated cluster of leveraged long positions between $60,000 and $62,000, raising concerns that another decline could trigger forced liquidations.

Meanwhile, CryptoQuant data show that large-holder accumulation has failed to offset broader distribution. However, several momentum indicators suggest Bitcoin price is oversold, as its moving-average structure continues to reflect a bearish trend.

Bitcoin Liquidation Heat Map Puts $60K–$62K in Focus

Glassnode’s liquidation heat map highlights a significant concentration of Bitcoin futures long positions between $60,000 and $62,000. These positions are associated with leveraged entries around the August breakout.

The chart highlights a significant concentration of Bitcoin futures long liquidations around $60,000–$62,000, linked to positions opened during the August breakout. Source: Glassndoe/X

Liquidation clusters identify price areas where leveraged traders could face forced position closures. If Bitcoin enters this zone, automatic liquidations could increase selling pressure and accelerate an existing decline.

While the $60,000–$62,000 range is not a confirmed downside target, the concentration of leveraged positions makes it a critical zone to monitor if Bitcoin’s selling pressure intensifies. Following weeks of November selling, traders are watching whether nearby support can hold or whether leveraged positions face another round of liquidations.

Recent Bitcoin Buyers Face Unrealized Losses

CryptoQuant reports that Bitcoin’s 24% decline has pushed recent buyers into negative unrealized returns. Their unrealized profits have fallen from approximately 35% in September to -15%, with an estimated on-chain cost basis of $80,300 against market prices near $65,000.

Bitcoin’s 24% decline has pushed recent buyers into losses, with unrealized returns falling from +35% in September to -15% as their $80,300 cost basis exceeds current prices near $65,000. Source: CryptoQuant/X

Wallet activity also reveals contrasting behavior among large holders. Addresses holding at least 1,000 BTC have accumulated approximately 47,000 BTC. However, wallets holding between 10 and 1,000 BTC have reduced their balances by around 65,000 BTC.

Negative US spot Bitcoin ETF flows and 30-day apparent demand of approximately -284,000 BTC add to the pressure. These figures suggest that accumulation among the largest holders has not been sufficient to offset broader distribution and weak market demand.

CryptoQuant identifies $68,700–$76,000 as an important resistance range. On the downside, $63,000 is a nearby support reference, while Bitcoin’s realized price near $53,800 represents a deeper on-chain level to monitor.

Bitcoin | Expanded Flat or Zigzag?

Elliott Wave analyst Mehdi_Abbasi_EWP identifies two possible interpretations of Bitcoin’s broader correction.

Bitcoin previously declined from $126,272 to approximately $57,870 before recovering toward $87,330. The latest downturn has created uncertainty over whether the recovery completed a corrective pattern or represented the first phase of a larger structure.

Bitcoin has developed a five-wave bearish Elliott Wave structure following its peak at $126,272. Source: Mehdi_Abbasi_EWP/TradingView

Scenario 1: Expanded Flat

Under the Expanded Flat interpretation, the recovery toward $87,330 may have completed Waves A and B, with the current decline beginning Wave C.

A five-wave bearish structure in the ongoing decline would support this scenario. A break below $57,870 would provide further confirmation.

The analyst identifies $45,863 and $34,615 as potential downside targets if this structure develops.

Scenario 2: Zigzag

The alternative interpretation views the advance from $57,870 to $87,330 as Wave A of a larger Zigzag correction.

Under this scenario, the current decline represents Wave B, leaving room for another corrective recovery before Wave C begins. The $95,000–$96,000 region, corresponding to the 38.2%–61.8% Fibonacci retracement zone, is an area to watch if buyers regain control.

However, the subsequent Wave C could still produce another decline, with $34,615 remaining a potential downside target.

The Structural Difference Between the Two Scenarios

The main distinction concerns whether the advance toward $87,330 completed an Expanded Flat’s corrective structure or represented the first wave of a larger Zigzag.

The internal wave structure and price behavior around $57,870 will help determine which interpretation is more consistent with market developments. Neither scenario is confirmed at this stage.

Bitcoin Technical Analysis: Oversold Signals Emerge Amid Bearish Momentum

Bitcoin trades near $65,458 in the supplied BITSTAMP technical snapshot, down approximately 2.49% in the latest session.

The overall technical summary shows a Sell signal, with 14 sell readings, five neutral, and seven buy signals. Moving averages carry a Strong Sell designation, while oscillators lean toward Buy as several momentum indicators enter oversold territory.

Bitcoin (BTC) price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) stands at 25, while the Stochastic %K is at 9 and the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) reads -215. These levels indicate substantial selling pressure and leave room for a potential short-term rebound.

However, the MACD remains negative at -3,499, while the Average Directional Index (ADX) stands at 31, indicating an established trend. The broader technical structure therefore remains bearish despite oversold readings.

Nearly all major moving averages sit above Bitcoin’s current price. The 10-day EMA is around $70,783, the 20-day EMA at $73,926, and the 50-day EMA near $77,094. The 200-day EMA stands at approximately $76,035.

These averages could create successive resistance barriers during a recovery. Bitcoin would need to reclaim the $70,000–$73,000 region before challenging higher levels.

Key Levels to Watch

Classic pivot calculations identify $80,274 as the central pivot, with resistance at $84,375, $91,321, and $102,367.

On the downside, support levels stand at:

  • $73,329: First support
  • $69,227: Second support
  • $58,181: Third support

These levels complement the $63,000 support identified by CryptoQuant. A sustained breakdown could expose Bitcoin to the previous low near $57,870 and the realized price around $53,800.

Bitcoin Price Outlook: Will $65K Hold or Will Sellers Target $60K?

Bitcoin’s immediate outlook depends on whether buyers can defend the $63,000–$65,000 region and restore demand. Glassnode’s $60,000–$62,000 liquidation cluster highlights the potential for additional volatility if selling accelerates.

On the upside, $68,700 is an important initial resistance, followed by the broader $70,000–$76,000 region. Oversold momentum indicators could support a temporary recovery, but stronger spot demand and improved ETF flows would be necessary to challenge the broader bearish structure.

For now, weak demand, negative momentum, and persistent distribution keep downside risks elevated. Bitcoin’s reaction around nearby support levels will help determine whether the latest decline stabilizes or develops into another leg lower.
