title: AI Tops Fed Survey of Financial Risks—Why Crypto Investors Should Pay Attention
summary: AI was the top concern in a new Fed survey of market contacts. The warning reaches beyond tech valuations to borrowing, cyber risk and the financial links crypto investors also depend on.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC CRWV NVDA

AI was the top concern in a new Fed survey of market contacts. The warning reaches beyond tech valuations to borrowing, cyber risk and the financial links crypto investors also depend on.

AI has become the most frequently cited financial-stability risk in a survey published with the Federal Reserve’s latest report, bringing the technology boom’s financing and market connections into sharper focus.

The November 13 Financial Stability Report says 87% of 23 market contacts surveyed in September and October cited AI, compared with 50% of 20 contacts in the spring. The concerns span valuations, cyber events and complicated financing arrangements.

For crypto investors, the significance lies in those channels of transmission. A shock does not need to originate inside Bitcoin to influence the people, lenders and trading infrastructure around it.

What the Fed AI risk figure actually measures

The report describes the survey box as a summary of respondents’ views. It says those views “should not be interpreted as representing the views of the Federal Reserve Board.”

That distinction prevents an eye-catching statistic becoming something it is not. An 87% response rate for a particular concern is not an 87% chance of a crisis, and the small sample is not a representative poll of all investors.

The collection period also matters. The answers were gathered before November’s latest market and corporate developments. They show concerns already present among financial professionals, rather than a measured reaction to the most recent headlines.

These are different survey groups at different times. The increase is a useful change in reported concern, but it cannot establish how each individual respondent changed their mind.

The financing question is bigger than whether AI works

A separate section of the report puts advanced-computing-related debt issuance above $680 billion by October 2026, compared with $130 billion in all of 2023. The figures concern issuance, rather than the same-period growth rate or the total value of the AI industry.

The investment question is therefore broader than model quality. A useful technology can attract spending that is poorly timed, too expensive or financed on terms that leave little room for disappointment. Strong demand and weak investment returns can coexist.

Consider a data-centre project that must pay lenders before customers deliver the expected cash. If deployment is delayed, the financing cost continues. A contract can support confidence in eventual demand while still leaving a cash-flow problem in the intervening months.

BNC’s CoreWeave earnings analysis offered a company-level example: rising revenue alongside substantial interest expense. The relevance is the relationship between growth and funding costs, rather than a claim that one company’s results establish a system-wide problem.

Why a technology shock can reach unrelated assets

One potential route is portfolio rebalancing. An investor facing losses in one position may reduce another to raise cash or meet a risk limit. That sale says something about the investor’s balance sheet, but not necessarily about the second asset’s fundamental prospects.

Another route is credit. If lenders reassess the risk of ambitious infrastructure projects, the cost or availability of financing can change. Companies dependent on fresh funding are more exposed to that adjustment than firms able to finance operations from existing cash generation.

For Bitcoin, those are reasons to monitor the broader financial setting. They are not proof that every AI stock decline must trigger a cryptocurrency sell-off. The size of the connection depends on who holds the positions, how they are financed and what other buyers are prepared to absorb.

Cyber risk is also a market-functioning issue

The Fed’s May financial-stability discussion had already described how attacks or software failures at financial institutions and third-party providers can impair services, weaken confidence and propagate through interconnected systems. The concern predates the latest survey.

That is particularly relevant to markets whose users depend on exchanges, custodians, cloud services and payment routes. A blockchain continuing to produce blocks does not ensure that every customer can reach an account, obtain a price or transfer money through an intermediary.

The practical question is where a critical dependency sits. If several firms rely on the same service, a disruption can reach them simultaneously. Resilience depends partly on alternatives, recovery arrangements and the ability to operate while one link is unavailable.

What investors should look for next

More useful evidence than another general warning would be clearer disclosure of borrowing terms, guarantees, customer concentration and the gap between construction spending and operating cash flow. Those details make it possible to judge who can withstand a disappointing quarter.

On the market side, distinguish a broad reduction in risk from an asset-specific reassessment. Prices, financing conditions and actual fund flows can help test that distinction when compared over matching periods. A correlation observed during one stressful week is not a permanent law.

The new survey does not settle whether AI is overvalued or predict the next crisis. It establishes that market contacts increasingly see the boom as a financial question as well as a technological one. For crypto readers, following the money and the dependencies may now be as useful as following the models.

title: Here’s what happened in crypto today
summary: Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
content:
Today in crypto, RWA protocol stUSDT is winding down operations, ending yield payments and giving tokenholders until May 2027 to redeem their assets. MegaETH co-founder Shuyao Kong said the restructuring affected employees who helped build the project’s blockchain, wallet and ecosystem, while OpenAI launched AI payments in ChatGPT.

RWA protocol stUSDT winds down three years after $2.3B TVL peak

Real-world asset (RWA) protocol stUSDT has begun winding down operations, nearly three years after reaching a $2.3 billion total value locked (TVL), ending rewards and opening a six-month redemption window for tokenholders. 

The team said that interest accrual on stUSDT ended on Saturday, with holders of stUSDT and its wrapped version, wstUSDT, able to redeem through its official portal until May 14, 2027. The team said requests submitted after the deadline will be handled through customer support in monthly batches through August 2027.

The team did not provide a reason for the shutdown but said all underlying assets remain fully backed. Holders with tokens on exchanges or DeFi platforms must transfer them to personal wallets before redeeming.

Cointelegraph reached out to stUSDT for more information but did not receive a response before publication. 

Meanwhile, JustLend DAO said it would phase out supply and borrowing functions for its wstUSDT market as part of the transition.

Launched in July 2023 on Tron, stUSDT allowed users to deposit USDT and earn yields from investments in real-world assets, including short-term government bonds. The protocol later expanded to Ethereum.

According to DefiLlama data, stUSDT’s TVL peaked at about $2.3 billion in November 2023 before declining substantially in subsequent years. It stood at about $8.6 million on Sunday, down from roughly $60 million a year earlier.

Despite its name, stUSDT is not affiliated with stablecoin issuer Tether. In September 2023, Tether denied any affiliation with stUSDT, saying the protocol was an independent project.

MegaETH parent cuts 20% of staff amid restructuring, AI push

MEGA, the organization behind Ethereum layer-2 network MegaETH, has reduced its workforce by 20% following months of restructuring as it expands into artificial intelligence products. 

On Friday, MegaETH co-founder Shuyao Kong said the organization had reorganized its teams, resulting in the departures of staff who worked on its blockchain, wallet, ecosystem support and communications. Kong did not disclose the number of employees affected or when the layoffs occurred. She said MEGA’s founders, early employees and core engineering team remain committed to the organization.

“We’ve brought together new capabilities and reorganized our teams, a process that has resulted in a 20% reduction in our staff,” Kong said. “These are people who helped build MEGA from its earliest days.”

The workforce reduction comes as MEGA shifts its focus toward developing products on the MegaETH network, including artificial intelligence services. The organization has committed $30 million to the initiative, although Kong did not directly link the layoffs to its new strategy.

In a whitepaper, MegaETH co-founders Yilong Li and Lei Yang outlined a proposed inference market aimed at giving users access to competing AI service providers. Their approach seeks to address concerns about whether providers use the advertised models and how they handle customer data.

Kong said MEGA plans to launch a public inference market in December.

OpenAI launches AI payments in ChatGPT with Visa, Mastercard and Amex

OpenAI on Friday introduced a new feature allowing AI agents to make purchases on behalf of users directly within ChatGPT through existing payment networks, in collaboration with American Express, Mastercard and Visa.

The wallet lets users authorize transactions using biometric verification, such as facial recognition or fingerprints. Payment networks generate tokenized card credentials for each approved purchase, keeping users’ actual card details from merchants and AI agents, the company said.

The service is being rolled out to ChatGPT Pro subscribers in the US with eligible cards issued in the country. OpenAI said it plans to eventually support purchases within preset spending limits and other restrictions without requiring approval for each transaction.

The launch comes as AI companies seek to move beyond product recommendations into executing transactions, potentially changing how consumers interact with online merchants. OpenAI said it is working with payment processors and fraud prevention firms to support AI purchases through existing checkout systems.

title: Bitcoin falls to four-month low near $62K as crypto selloff deepens
summary: The global cryptocurrency market capitalization fell 4% to $2.26 trillion over 24 hours, while Ether and Solana posted double-digit weekly losses.
content:
MarketsPublishedNov 15, 2026

The global cryptocurrency market capitalization fell 4% to $2.26 trillion over 24 hours, while Ether and Solana posted double-digit weekly losses.

Bitcoin fell to a four-month low near $62,000 on Sunday, extending a selloff across major digital assets before recovering some of its losses.

On Sunday, Bitcoin (BTC) dropped to a 24-hour low of $62,080.91, according to CoinGecko, its weakest level since July. The asset later rebounded above $65,000 but remained down nearly 15% in the last seven days. 

The downturn extended beyond Bitcoin. CoinGecko data showed Ether (ETH) down 19.5% over the past week, while Solana (SOL) lost 20.7%. The total value of the cryptocurrency market fell about 4% over 24 hours to $2.26 trillion, according to CoinGecko. 

Market sentiment also deteriorated. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index fell to 10 on Sunday from 13 on Saturday and 20 on Friday, remaining in “extreme fear,” according to Alternative.me.

The move followed Friday’s slide below $70,000, as analysts reported weakening investor sentiment and concerns over institutional outflows and tighter liquidity.

The latest decline came after US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks. The funds lost $1.07 billion during the week ended Nov. 13, following $1.28 billion the previous week. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust extended its outflow streak to 11 trading sessions on Friday.

title: Initia Cloud Breach Triggers Forged IBC Withdrawals Across Five Rollups
summary:
Key Takeaways: After successfully breaching Initia’s cloud environment, an attacker made around $3.27 million. However, around $2.16mn is stuck on paused Layer 1, and isn’t moving any further on Initia.
The post Initia Cloud Breach Triggers Forged IBC Withdrawals Across Five Rollups appeared first o...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • After successfully breaching Initia’s cloud environment, an attacker made around $3.27 million.
  • However, around $2.16mn is stuck on paused Layer 1, and isn’t moving any further on Initia.
  • The attacker siphoned 5 amounts of IBC withdrawals from five rollups, and according to Initia, it will rebuild the funds of affected assets in full.

Initia has revealed new information regarding breaches on its cloud credentials that led it to infrastructure of rollups on its Layer 1. It’s the second time that Initia has suffered a big security breach in three weeks, following an unrelated exploitation in October.

Based on our investigation so far, on November 9th an attacker gained unauthorized access to Initia’s infrastructure through a command injection attack with a compromised GCP key used for provisioning private nodes. This exposed environment variables, which allowed the attacker to access our GitHub and GCP accounts and obtain further credentials.

With these credentials the attacker gained access to Anvil, the hosting platform used by rollups on Initia. Through this the attacker was able to validate forged IBC withdrawals from five rollups, unlocking assets held by the Initia L1’s IBC escrow accounts.

Around $3.27m of assets were moved to the attacker’s Initia L1 address with $2.16m of the stolen funds remaining on the paused L1 where they cannot be moved. The attacker sold stolen assets on the Initia DEX and then withdrew 13.4k TIA, 8k USDC.inj, and 597k Noble USDC reaching Initia’s outbound IBC rate limits. No INIT was withdrawn from Initia by the attacker.

We intend to restore the backing of affected assets in full. We are finalizing the plan and will share the details once it is confirmed.

As a precaution, we are rebuilding the affected infrastructure from scratch in an isolated environment, enforcing least-privilege access controls, and hardening security at every layer of the stack from cloud infrastructure to onchain IBC validation. Given the above, we expect this process to be longer than a routine network restart. We will share timelines as they become available.

All announcements will be made through Initia’s official channels. Thank you for your patience.

— Initia 🪢 (@initia) November 10, 2026

  • Compromised GCP Key Opened the Door
  • Forged IBC Withdrawals Released $3.27M
    • Initia Rebuilds Infrastructure Before Network Restart

Compromised GCP Key Opened the Door

The compromise was performed on Nov. 9 using an Initia-provisioned key on Google Cloud Platform to gain control of the private nodes through command injection, Initia found.

The access exposed environment variables, which were then used to access Initia’s GitHub and GCP accounts to gain further access. The attacker then connected to the Initia hosting platform rollups use (Anvil).

Subsequently, fraudulent Inter-Blockchain Communication withdrawals were then double-validated on five rollups before the assets were untethered on Initia’s Layer 1.

Read More: Mercado Bitcoin Freezes Deposits and Withdrawals After $40M Crypto Security Alert

Forged IBC Withdrawals Released $3.27M

Nearly $3.27 million worth of assets were sent to the attacker’s L1 address, Initia noted.

The attacker then sold some of the stolen assets through Initia’s decentralized exchange and withdrew 13,400 TIA, 8,000 USDC.inj and 597,000 Noble USDC before hitting the network’s outbound IBC rate limits.

Importantly, Initia said the withdrawal of INIT tokens did not occur. There are over $2.16 million in assets on Layer 1 that aren’t transferable at this time.

Initia Rebuilds Infrastructure Before Network Restart

Initia said it plans to completely recover the backing of any impacted assets and is developing a recovery plan.

In addition to the usual switch on, the team is rebuilding the damaged infrastructure from the ground up in an isolated environment. It additionally hopes to implement more rigorous least-privilege access controls and improve security in its cloud systems by on-chain IBC validation.

The network might stay off for an extended time, then, as during an ordinary disruption. They are also continuing with their asset recovery with Law Enforcement and Security partners.

The leak comes after a hackers exploit on Oct. 23 which saw the attackers defraud around $2.7 million from the company using a MoveVM script cache vulnerability. That earlier incident enabled credentials to be created and cross-chain withdrawals made without any authorization prior to the network being paused.

The two attacks were different in that the former was based on migration issues involving the blockchain execution logic and the current attack led to an off-chain breach of cloud infrastructure and was only recognised by its entry into rollup or IBC systems.

title: Hidden Implants Found in Three Trezor Wallets—Why a Firmware Update Is Not Enough
summary: Trezor has identified implants in three Safe 5 wallets bought from former reseller CryptoBilis. Its latest findings explain why blocking the hardware does not undo a leaked wallet backup.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Trezor has identified implants in three Safe 5 wallets bought from former reseller CryptoBilis. Its latest findings explain why blocking the hardware does not undo a leaked wallet backup.

A Trezor wallet investigation has identified hidden hardware implants in three Safe 5 devices bought from former reseller CryptoBilis, sharpening a warning that software alone cannot undo an already exposed recovery phrase.

In its November 12 investigation update, Trezor said one device had been examined in its lab and two others identified through owners’ photographs. The three purchases took place between August 20 and September 23 through CryptoBilis directly and its Tokopedia and Shopee stores.

The company says none of those owners has lost funds and that it has found no confirmed cases involving another reseller or Trezor model. The finding is consequential, but its scope is specific. It does not establish that Trezor wallets generally contain the implant.

The Trezor wallet warning has moved beyond an initial report

The company’s October 30 notice described a credible allegation that it had not yet verified by examining the reported device. The latest findings move that case forward, while retaining an important distinction between a laboratory examination and identification from photographs.

That is why three identified devices should not become three laboratory-confirmed examinations in retellings of the story. Equally, the absence of reported losses should not be mistaken for proof that an exposed backup is safe.

The investigation remains a supply-chain story: what happened to particular devices before they reached their owners. The evidence does not identify the people responsible, and the fact that a device passed through a reseller is not by itself proof of who altered it.

A compromised display can undermine a secure device

Trezor’s original notice described an additional board between the main electronics and the display, with a cellular module and antenna. The concern was that it could capture recovery words shown during setup and transmit them over a mobile network.

The crucial point for users is the role of the backup. A hardware wallet protects signing keys, but its recovery phrase is designed to restore access elsewhere. If an attacker learns that phrase, replacing the physical device while retaining the same backup does not remove that knowledge.

This is a different failure mode from malicious firmware changing what a wallet does. Extra hardware can target information displayed during a legitimate operation. A device can therefore appear to function normally while the secret needed to recreate the wallet is no longer private.

Why the firmware fix does not settle the backup question

Trezor says firmware 2.13.1, released on November 11, blocks the implants it has identified from capturing further information. Its guidance for CryptoBilis buyers nevertheless remains to move funds to “a new wallet with a new seed.”

A patch addresses future behaviour on the updated device. It cannot make an attacker forget a recovery phrase captured earlier. Those are different security tasks, and treating one as a substitute for the other would leave the central exposure unresolved.

For the same reason, a backup restored onto a newly purchased device can preserve the old risk. What needs replacing is the potentially compromised secret as well as the hardware used to manage it.

There is no need to publish that secret to establish whether a purchase came from the affected seller. Purchase records and official support can address provenance without exposing the information that controls the funds.

Who should act, and where should they verify instructions?

The earlier notice applies precautionary guidance to all Trezor models bought through CryptoBilis from March 2026 onwards, including marketplace stores supplied by that reseller. Devices not yet set up should not be initialised or given an existing recovery phrase.

Users unsure about the source of a device should start with receipts and Trezor’s official support channel. The company’s replacement arrangements are described in its investigation update. A suspicious device should be kept and left unused while support advises on the next steps.

The October notice also warns about scammers exploiting the incident through fake messages, letters and phone calls. It states: “Trezor Support will never ask for it,” referring to the wallet backup. A purported rescue request for recovery words is therefore a warning sign, not a verification procedure.

The broader lesson is about custody, not panic

BNC’s coverage of the Binance recovery and social-engineering threats showed how asset security can fail outside a blockchain’s consensus rules. This case adds a physical route: the equipment entrusted with a secret can itself be altered.

For self-custody users, provenance and recovery procedures belong alongside password hygiene and software updates. A sealed-looking package or a familiar marketplace name cannot answer every question about where a device has been.

The useful response is proportionate to the evidence: identify the seller, follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the affected purchases and protect recovery words from anyone offering unsolicited help. Trezor’s narrow findings warrant a precise warning. They do not justify either dismissing the risk or telling every owner their wallet has been compromised.

title: XTB Now Holds 42% of Poland's Brokerage Accounts, Up From 30%
summary:
XTB's share of Poland's brokerage accounts reached about 42% at the end of October, up from roughly 30% a year earlier. The Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW) published the figures on Monday.
The Warsaw-listed broker ran more than 1.336 million of the market's 3.155 million accounts. In ...
content:
2026-11-15T10:16:00.000+02:00

Sunday, 15/11/2026 | 08:16 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • It opened about 50,900 of the 64,416 added in October, according to the national securities depository.
  • Openings at other firms rose 28% from September, while XTB's own intake ran 13% below last October.

XTB's share of Poland's brokerage accounts reached about 42% at the end of October, up from roughly 30% a year earlier. The Central Securities Depository of Poland (KDPW) published the figures on Monday.

The Warsaw-listed broker ran more than 1.336 million of the market's 3.155 million accounts. In October alone it opened about 50,900 of the 64,416 accounts added across all firms, or 79%, by FinanceMagnates.com's calculation from the KDPW figures.

Over 12 months, XTB added 620,262 of the 774,795 new accounts in the market, about four in five, the same share it took in October 2025. Its count is now more than twice that of mBank's brokerage arm, the second-largest, at just under 589,000.

The market as a whole grew about 33% in that time. KDPW counted 2,856,520 accounts in May, FM Intelligence data show, and nearly 300,000 have been added since.

London's trading industry is coming home!

Accounts in Poland, Clients Abroad

The KDPW count covers securities accounts with access to the Polish market, so it leaves out XTB's foreign clients. Worldwide, XTB reported more than 100,600 new clients in October's first 27 days, about 5% more than a year earlier.

title: Coinone warns of phishing, identity theft after customer data breach
summary: The South Korean crypto exchange said potentially exposed information includes passwords, bank account numbers, national identification numbers and crypto wallet addresses.
content:
Latest NewsPublishedNov 15, 2026

The South Korean crypto exchange said potentially exposed information includes passwords, bank account numbers, national identification numbers and crypto wallet addresses.

South Korean crypto exchange Coinone warned customers of potential phishing scams and identity theft after an attacker breached its outsourced customer support provider, exposing information shared during customer service interactions. 

On Sunday, Coinone said an attacker accessed servers operated by MetaM on Thursday and viewed or extracted customer support records. Coinone said it learned about the breach in the same day. 

According to Coinone, the information potentially exposed names, phone numbers, email addresses, dates of birth, bank account numbers, passwords, national identification numbers, home and wallet addresses and transaction IDs. 

Coinone said the affected data varies by customer, and people who never contacted its support center were unaffected. It did not disclose how many customers were affected. 

The exchange urged customers who shared passwords during support interactions to change them and warned that fraudsters could impersonate Coinone using details from previous conversations. 

Coinone said its account, trading and wallet infrastructure operates separately from MetaM’s servers, with no evidence of direct compromise. The exchange said it has reported the incident to South Korean authorities. 

The disclosure comes as South Korea moves to strengthen financial-sector cybersecurity. In October, the Financial Services Commission identified security deficiencies at 130 of 555 financial firms reviewed.

On Thursday, the regulator said it would allow crypto exchanges to suspend withdrawals when hacking is suspected, alongside calls for round-the-clock monitoring.

title: RWA protocol stUSDT winds down three years after $2.3B TVL peak
summary: The stUSDT team did not disclose a reason for winding down the RWA protocol but assured holders that all underlying assets remain fully backed.
content:
Real-world asset (RWA) protocol stUSDT has begun winding down operations, nearly three years after reaching a $2.3 billion total value locked (TVL), ending rewards and opening a six-month redemption window for tokenholders. 

The team said that interest accrual on stUSDT ended on Saturday, with holders of stUSDT and its wrapped version, wstUSDT, able to redeem through its official portal until May 14, 2027. The team said requests submitted after the deadline will be handled through customer support in monthly batches through August 2027.

The team did not provide a reason for the shutdown but said all underlying assets remain fully backed. Holders with tokens on exchanges or DeFi platforms must transfer them to personal wallets before redeeming.

Cointelegraph reached out to stUSDT for more information but did not receive a response before publication. 

Meanwhile, JustLend DAO said it would phase out supply and borrowing functions for its wstUSDT market as part of the transition.

Launched in July 2023 on Tron, stUSDT allowed users to deposit USDT and earn yields from investments in real-world assets, including short-term government bonds. The protocol later expanded to Ethereum.

According to DefiLlama data, stUSDT’s TVL peaked at about $2.3 billion in November 2023 before declining substantially in subsequent years. It stood at about $8.6 million on Sunday, down from roughly $60 million a year earlier.

Despite its name, stUSDT is not affiliated with stablecoin issuer Tether. In September 2023, Tether denied any affiliation with stUSDT, saying the protocol was an independent project.

Binance Staking Review: What Is It?

Crypto staking on Binance involves locking digital assets to support a blockchain network’s security and earn rewards. This system is called Proof-of-Stake (PoS), and when you stake your crypto, you are mainly helping to verify and add new transactions to the blockchain.

Unlike mining, staking requires no hardware or energy. No hardware or energy is required. You just need to hold your coins on the platform, and Binance manages technical processes. You only need to choose the coin and the staking period.

Binance offers both types of staking: Locked Staking and Flexible Staking. Locked means your funds stay locked for a few days or weeks, and flexible means you can unstake your funds anytime. Locked staking typically yields higher rewards.

Binance vs. Binance.US Staking: What Are the Differences?

Binance and Binance.US both offer crypto staking services to their users, but have some differences. Global Binance supports more than 100 coins for staking, so you can stake coins like BNB, ADA, DOT, SOL, and many others. Binance.US gives fewer choices, and to be exact, it supports around 20 coins only.

Global Binance distributes staking rewards daily or weekly, depending on the coin. On Binance.US, most rewards are paid weekly. Additionally, APR varies between platforms. Binance generally offers high APRs due to its support for more niche coins, which you won’t find on the Binance.US platform.

Binance charges a lower staking fee compared to Binance.US. On global Binance, the fee can go up to 10% of your rewards, which is quite reasonable. But on Binance.US, the fee is much higher; it can range between 9.95% and even go up to 39.95%, depending on the coin you stake.

What Are the Benefits of Staking on Binance?

The benefits of staking on Binance are earning passive income, easy usage, supporting the network, having many crypto options, and not needing to run a validator node.

  • Earn Passive Income: One main benefit is that you can earn more cryptocurrency without doing much work. Your crypto earns rewards just by staying in your Binance account, and this can be seen as an effective method to grow your cryptocurrency holdings.
  • Easy to Use: Binance makes staking very simple. You do not need to have special computer skills or equipment. You just have to choose the crypto you want to stake on the platform and confirm it with a few clicks.
  • Support the Network: You actively strengthen blockchain network security by staking your cryptocurrency. Your staked assets are used to verify transactions and keep the network safe.
  • Many Crypto Options: Binance offers staking for a lot of different cryptocurrencies, over 100 coins. You can choose which coin you want to stake based on what you have and the rewards offered. They also have different staking periods, like flexible or locked.
  • No Need to Run a Node: You do not need to set up any validator or system. Binance handles everything for you, and you only need to hold coins in your account.

What Are the Limitations of Binance Staking?

The limitations of Binance staking include lock-up periods, market changes, limited new coin support, slow unstaking, and changing reward rates.

  • Lock-up Periods: Sometimes, when you stake your crypto, it gets locked for a certain time. During this period, you cannot move or sell your staked coins. Thus, this can be an issue if you need your funds quickly. For some coins, Binance allows you to unstake before maturity, but in this case, you have to return your earned staking rewards. 
  • Market Volatility: The value of your staked cryptocurrency can go up or down very fast. Even if you earn rewards, if the price of the coin drops a lot, the value of your total investment might still be lower. The market can be very uncertain.
  • Limited Availability for Some Coins: While Binance offers many options, not every single cryptocurrency can be staked. Additionally, staking spots for popular coins may become unavailable quickly, and this means you might not always find a spot for the specific coin you want to stake.
  • Unstaking Time: When you decide to stop staking and get your coins back, there can be a waiting period. This is called the unstaking period. During this time, your coins are not available for use, and you do not earn any new rewards. The unstaking period varies by the coin you staked.
  • Reward Rates Change: The APR is not fixed. It can go up or down at any time. This makes it hard to guess how much you will earn.

What Are Binance Staking Rewards and Rates?

Binance staking rewards are the profits you earn for locking your crypto on the Binance platform. The reward is usually displayed as Annual Percentage Rate (APR), an estimated annual return. So, some coins give 10% APR, and some give 15% or more. But this rate can change at any time. Here are Binance staking rates for some popular coins (at the time of writing):

CoinsStaking APR (Simple Earn)
USD Coin (USDC)11.61%
Tether (USDT)12.2%
Ethereum (ETH)1.24%
Solana (SOL)5.1%
Polkadot (DOT)5.8%
Cardano (ADA)2.1%

How Does Binance Staking Rewards Work?

Binance staking rewards work by giving you earnings for holding certain coins on the platform. When you stake a cryptocurrency, Binance secures it for you. They then use your locked coin to secure the blockchain network. You don’t need to do any difficult technical stuff yourself; Binance handles all that for you. Because your coins help this network stay safe and run smoothly, you get rewards back.

These rewards are actually distributed through the blockchain network itself, not directly from Binance. Binance just helps to collect these rewards and then sends them to your account.

The amount of reward depends on the coin, the network rules, and how much you stake. Some coins pay higher, and some pay lower. Binance also shows you an Annual Percentage Rate (APR), which is like an estimated yearly return, before you start. But remember, this APR can change and is not a fixed number. Some rewards are paid daily, and some are weekly. 

Binance has two main ways to stake. One is called flexible staking, and the other is locked staking. Your coins are held for a set amount of time with locked staking, like 30 or 90 days, and you usually get bigger rewards for this. Flexible staking lets you withdraw your coins almost any time you want, but the rewards are often smaller. 

Binance also takes a small fee from the rewards you earn, which is generally around 10%. Once staking ends, your coins and rewards are returned to your Binance wallet.

What Are the Types of Staking on Binance?

The types of staking on Binance are locked staking, DeFi staking, ETH 2.0 staking, and flexible staking.

Locked Staking

Locked Staking on Binance is a method of receiving higher rewards for your crypto holdings. When you opt for locked staking (also called fixed-term staking), you mainly commit to leaving your crypto locked in a Binance account for an agreed duration. This duration can be, for instance, 30 days, 60 days, or 90 days. 

You are not allowed to transfer or sell your coins during the locked duration. Since your coins are being locked for a predetermined time, the rewards earned by you are generally higher. This is reflected in the form of a higher Annual Percentage Rate (APR). It implies that more comes back to you compared to flexible staking.

This style of staking is great if you are going to keep your coins for the long term in any case. It lets you get more value from your crypto while it’s sitting idle. The terms of each locked staking product will indicate to you the actual lock-up period and the APR you can receive. At the end of the selected period, your initial staked quantity and the rewards you earned are transferred back to your spot wallet.

DeFi Staking

DeFi Staking on Binance enables you to participate in decentralized finance (DeFi) projects. You can participate via Binance, avoiding complex technical processes. DeFi projects are based on blockchain and can provide services such as lending or borrowing cryptocurrency, all without involving banks. Using Binance’s DeFi staking, Binance links your cryptocurrency to these third-party DeFi protocols.

Binance manages complex tasks, selecting reliable DeFi projects. You just need to place your cryptocurrency in Binance’s DeFi staking program, and Binance becomes the intermediary to these decentralized services. 

You will then receive rewards from these DeFi protocols in return. Hence, this makes it easier and safer for normal users to get involved in DeFi. Binance selects reliable DeFi protocols, though risks such as smart contract vulnerabilities remain.

ETH 2.0 Staking

ETH 2.0 Staking, which is now referred to as Ethereum’s Beacon Chain staking, is mainly a way to support the upgrade of the Ethereum network. Binance provides an easy means of getting involved in it. When you stake your Ethereum (ETH) into ETH 2.0 via Binance, your ETH is locked up for an extremely long period of time. It will remain locked until the entire Ethereum network upgrade is complete, something that could take a couple of years.

Because of this extended lock-up, Binance provides a unique BETH token. If you stake ETH for ETH 2.0, you receive BETH at a 1:1 ratio in return. BETH is a token that represents your staked ETH along with whatever rewards you accumulate. Binance takes care of all the technical requirements of ETH 2.0 staking so that users can easily join.

Flexible Staking

Flexible Staking on Binance is an extremely simple method of getting some rewards from your cryptocurrency. Unlike locked staking, flexible staking allows withdrawals without a fixed duration. This implies that you can put your crypto in for staking and withdraw it almost at any time you desire. There is no significant lock-up period. This is ideal for accessing coins for trading or other uses.

The key advantage is the ease of withdrawing your money. But since you can withdraw your coins at will, the rewards you get are typically lower compared to locked staking. The Annual Percentage Yield (APY) of flexible staking tends to be lower. This is suitable for users who wish to receive some extra from their unused crypto but would like to keep their money readily available.

How to Stake and Unstake on Binance?

To stake on Binance, you need to log in and find the staking section, then choose your staking type and the specific coin, input the amount to stake and confirm the details, and finally, monitor your staking activity and rewards.

To unstake on Binance, you need to go to your staking page and initiate the redemption, then wait for the required unstaking period (which is up to 24 hours for some coins), and finally, receive your crypto back in your wallet.

Step-by-Step Guide to Staking on Binance

Step 1: Log In and Find Staking Section

First, you need to open your web browser and go to the official Binance website. If you are not already logged in, enter your email or phone number and your password to sign in to your Binance account. Also, if you are new, learn everything about the exchange in our honest and detailed Binance review, and register using our Binance referral code to get a $100 welcome bonus.

Once logged in, navigate to the top menu bar to find options like ‘Trade,’ ‘Earn,’ and more. Move your mouse over the “Earn” button. A drop-down menu will appear. In this menu, look for an option that says “Simple Earn”. Click on this. This will take you to the main staking page.

Step 2: Choose Your Staking Type and Coin

Now, here on the Binance Staking page, you will see different types of staking available. As discussed above, the most common ones are “Locked Staking” and “Flexible Staking”.Then you can select your preferred staking type from the available options.

Review the list of cryptocurrencies available for staking, each displaying the Annual Percentage Rate (APR), which is the estimated yearly reward, and also the available periods for locked staking. You should choose the cryptocurrency you want to stake and the staking type that fits your needs, and then click on the coin you want to stake.

Step 3: Input Staking Amount and Confirm

After you choose your coin, a new window or page will open, and here, you need to enter the amount of cryptocurrency you want to stake. There will be a box where you can type in the number of coins. Also, you must review the minimum and maximum staking amounts for your chosen coin before staking.

You will also see details about the staking period (if it’s locked staking), the estimated APR, and when your rewards will be paid. And, make sure to read the staking rules and agreements carefully. These rules explain things like unstaking times or any special conditions. After you have checked all the details and are happy with them, click the “Confirm” button. This will start your staking.

Step 4: Monitor Your Staking and Rewards

Once you have started staking, you can easily check its status. Go back to your Binance account dashboard, and then, look for sections like “Simple Earn”. This page will show you all your active staking products.

Here, you can see how much crypto you have staked, the rewards you have earned so far, and the time remaining if it is locked staking. Rewards are automatically sent to your Spot Wallet daily or weekly. You can monitor your rewards’ growth.

How to Unstake and Redeem on Binance?

To unstake or redeem your staked coins on Binance, you need to visit the “Simple Earn” page again. For flexible staking or early locked staking redemption (where permitted), visit the Simple Earn page. Find the active staking product and look for an “Unstake” button.

Now, click it and follow the steps to confirm, and also remember, there might be a short unstaking period before the coins are fully returned to your Spot Wallet. Unstaking period is generally around 24 hours for some coins. Also, for a full locked staking period, your principal amount and earned rewards are often returned to your Spot Wallet automatically after the period ends.

Is Staking Safe on Binance?

Yes, staking on Binance is generally considered safe, as Binance is a large and well-known cryptocurrency exchange with over 250 million users. They use strong security methods to protect user funds, like two-factor authentication and keeping most funds in “cold storage” (offline wallets), and Binance also has a Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), which can help cover losses in case of a security breach. However, staking involves risks beyond Binance’s control, such as market volatility. The value of the crypto you stake can go down due to market changes.

title: Bitcoin ETFs Shed $2.35 Billion in Two Weeks as BlackRock’s Outflow Streak Hits 11
summary: Two consecutive billion-dollar outflow weeks leave Bitcoin’s institutional demand under pressure. BlackRock’s IBIT accounts for most of the latest withdrawals, but the numbers need careful reading.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Two consecutive billion-dollar outflow weeks leave Bitcoin’s institutional demand under pressure. BlackRock’s IBIT accounts for most of the latest withdrawals, but the numbers need careful reading.

Bitcoin ETF outflows have reached $2.347 billion across the first two completed November trading weeks, leaving a persistent hole in one of the market’s most closely watched sources of demand.

BNC’s calculations from Farside Investors’ fund-flow table show $1.0653 billion leaving U.S. spot Bitcoin funds during November 9–13, following $1.2817 billion in the preceding week. BlackRock’s IBIT recorded withdrawals on every session in both weeks and on October 30, extending its losing streak to 11 trading days.

The figures describe net investor flows through the products. They do not mean BlackRock’s corporate treasury has decided to sell its own Bitcoin holdings, or establish that every departing investor has abandoned cryptocurrency altogether.

Bitcoin ETF outflows remain concentrated in IBIT

IBIT accounted for $908.4 million of the latest week’s net withdrawals, about 85% of the industry total. Its November withdrawals through Friday reached $2.118 billion, approximately 90% of the combined net outflow across the funds.

Concentration matters when interpreting the headline. One very large product can drive the aggregate even while some competing funds attract money. An industry total does not show that every provider or customer group is moving in the same direction.

Friday’s $185.4 million net withdrawal was smaller than Thursday’s $284.1 million. But a less negative session remains a negative session. It is evidence that the pace changed, rather than confirmation that demand has recovered.

The industry’s losing run is shorter than IBIT’s: seven sessions, beginning November 5. On November 4, the combined funds attracted $74.6 million even as IBIT lost money. That is a concrete example of why a fund-specific streak and an industry-wide streak should not be used interchangeably. The totals here use the table as checked on November 15; automated flow datasets can subsequently be revised.

A large fund is still a large fund

The iShares product page reported IBIT net assets of approximately $54.13 billion as of November 13. Its net asset value was $39.00 per share, while its closing market price was $38.94.

Those figures put the withdrawals beside a substantial remaining investor base. They also illustrate why assets under management and fund flows should not be treated as interchangeable: assets can shrink because Bitcoin falls, because investors redeem shares, or through a combination of both.

Likewise, trading volume in ETF shares is not automatically a net inflow. Shares can change hands between buyers and sellers on an exchange without the product receiving an equivalent amount of new capital. That distinction becomes particularly useful during volatile sessions.

Reading the market therefore requires separate questions: how much exposure investors retain, how much new money enters or leaves, and how the underlying asset is priced. One dramatic number cannot answer all three.

BlackRock’s longer-term argument faces a near-term test

BlackRock has previously argued that weak flows do not necessarily overturn Bitcoin’s long-term investment case. In an earlier research paper using data through mid-2026, its digital-assets team described the pullback’s pressures as “cyclical flow dynamics.”

The paper, co-authored by Robert Mitchnick, Will Su and Alice Wang, separated episodes of leveraged selling and slowing institutional demand from its case for Bitcoin as a longer-term portfolio diversifier. It also discussed competition for capital from AI-themed investments.

That research predates the November withdrawals. It should be read as the manager’s investment framework, not a fresh explanation of this particular week. BlackRock also sponsors IBIT, giving readers a reason to distinguish its commercial perspective from the independently tabulated flows.

The tension is useful rather than contradictory. A long-term thesis can remain intact in an investor’s view while near-term allocations decline. The practical test is whether that conviction eventually translates into renewed purchases.

The macro backdrop adds another hurdle

BNC’s analysis of the latest wholesale inflation release examined the distinction between a slower monthly increase and persistent annual price pressure. For Bitcoin, the relevant channel is how that evidence influences financing conditions and willingness to hold risk.

The ETF figures cannot isolate inflation, sentiment or any other single cause of redemptions. Nor do they reveal whether investors are reducing leverage, changing vehicles, raising cash or making a permanent allocation decision. Those explanations require evidence beyond the daily totals.

What would signal a more durable improvement?

The next useful development would be sustained net buying across several sessions, ideally involving more than one fund. A single positive day could interrupt a streak without changing the wider demand picture.

It would also help to compare fund flows with spot trading and derivatives positioning over matching dates. A weekend Bitcoin move takes place while U.S. fund shares are not in their normal trading session; it should not be described as a new daily ETF-flow reading.

For now, the completed-week data show repeated withdrawals from a major access route into Bitcoin. The important question for the next trading week is whether that drain slows convincingly—and whether buyers return in sufficient size to turn stabilisation into fresh demand.

Binance Spot Trading Review – What Is It and How Does It Work?

Binance spot trading is a service that lets you buy and sell digital assets at current market prices on one of the world’s biggest cryptocurrency exchanges. There is no leverage or borrowing involved. Binance also supports automated strategies such as Spot Grid Trading Bots.

Today, Binance has become the world’s largest crypto exchange with over 280 million users in more than a hundred countries, and you can choose from 500+ cryptocurrencies and over 1,500 trading pairs. Liquidity is deep because millions of traders are buying and selling around the clock, so trades generally execute quickly with minimal slippage.

Spot trading works based on an order book. You need to deposit fiat currency or another crypto asset into your Binance wallet and select a trading pair, such as BTC/USDT. The order book shows bids (buyers) and asks (sellers). You have to decide how many tokens you want and choose the price, or use a market order to accept the best available price. When your order matches with an opposite order from another user, the exchange executes the trade and updates your balance immediately. Binance charges a small fee for executing the order, which starts at 0.1% for both makers and takers. 

After the trade, the platform credits your new asset balance and debits the one you sold. You can withdraw tokens to your own wallet or keep them on the exchange. The platform also offers additional tools such as charts, technical indicators, and trading bots.

What Are the Pros and Cons of Spot Trading on Binance?

Pros of Spot Trading on Binance

The pros of spot trading on Binance are deep liquidity, competitive trading fees, a wide selection of assets, a large integrated ecosystem, spot trading bots, and advanced trading features.

  • Deep liquidity: The exchange has billions of dollars of spot trading volume daily. With so much activity on each trading pair, your orders are likely to be filled quickly, and price slippage stays low even for larger trades. Tight spreads mean you can enter and exit positions efficiently.
  • Low and flexible fees: Spot trading fees start at 0.1% for makers and takers. You can reduce your costs by paying fees with BNB tokens, which provides a 25% discount, or by climbing through the VIP tiers based on your 30‑day trading volume. Some popular pairs, such as BTC/FDUSD, trade with zero maker and taker fees.
  • Wide selection of assets: There are more than 500 cryptocurrencies and 1,500 spot trading pairs, giving you exposure to major coins like Bitcoin and Ethereum, plus a long list of altcoins. The exchange lists new coins regularly, so you can access trending tokens without opening accounts on multiple exchanges.
  • Integrated ecosystem: Binance offers more than just spot trading. You can stake tokens via Binance Earn, pay merchants through Binance Pay, learn via Binance Academy, and participate in community discussions on Binance Square.
  • Advanced tools: The platform provides charting tools, API access, and different order types (market, limit, stop‑limit, trailing stop, and OCO). Also, more experienced traders can integrate bots or algorithms, while beginners can use the simple buy/sell interface.
  • Binance Trading Bots: Binance’s automated trading bots can simplify strategies. You can set them to follow dollar-cost averaging or other presets for steady market entry or use other preset strategies for buying and selling.

Cons of Spot Trading on Binance

The cons of spot trading on Binance include a lack of full decentralization, potential regulatory restrictions, and a complex interface for beginners.

  • Not Fully Decentralized: You do not own your private keys when trading on Binance. Your funds are stored on the exchange, which carries custody risk, and if the platform faces issues, withdrawals can be delayed.
  • Potential regulatory restrictions: Binance spot trading access is limited in certain regions. Binance’s terms of use restrict customers in the United States, Canada (Ontario), Iran, Cuba, Crimea, and North Korea. Residents of these jurisdictions must look for alternatives or use local versions of the platform, such as Binance.US, which offers fewer coins.
  • Complex Interface for Beginners: The platform’s advanced features can feel overwhelming for new traders. Charts, multiple order types, and settings may cause confusion. So, beginners might take time to adapt.

Binance Spot Trading Order Types

Binance spot trading order types are market order, limit order, OCO order, trailing-stop order, and stop-limit order.

Binance Market Order

A market order buys or sells instantly at the best available price on the order book. So, when you place one, the exchange matches your order with existing bids. Because you accept the current market price, there is no guarantee on the exact fill price, and taker fees apply. Market orders are useful when immediate execution is more important than the price.

Binance Limit Order

A limit order lets you set a specific price at which you want to buy or sell. The order remains in the book until the market reaches your chosen price, and if the price never reaches your limit, the order remains unfilled. Limit orders give you control over entry and exit prices, often at lower maker fees, and they provide liquidity to other traders.

Binance One-Cancels-the-Other (OCO) Order

An OCO order combines a limit order and a stop‑limit order. When one part of the pair executes, the other cancels automatically. Hence, this setup mainly allows you to place a take‑profit limit order and a stop‑loss order simultaneously.

Binance Trailing-Stop Order

A trailing‑stop order follows the market price at a fixed percentage or amount. So, if the price moves in your favor, the stop level moves with it, locking in potential profits. And when the price reverses by the specified trail amount, the order triggers and sells (or buys) at market, protecting gains. Trailing stops are valuable in trending markets where you want to let profits run while limiting potential losses.

Binance Stop Limit Order

A stop‑limit order uses two prices: a stop price that triggers the order and a limit price that defines the worst price you are willing to accept. When the market hits the stop price, the system places a limit order at your limit price. Mainly, this order type is helpful for setting precise stop‑losses or trigger‑based entries where you don’t want slippage beyond your limit.

Is Spot Trading on Binance Safe to Use in 2025?

Yes, Binance spot trading is safe to use because the exchange invests heavily in protective measures and provides transparency around its reserves. The company publishes Proof‑of‑Reserves reports showing that user assets are fully backed 1:1 with additional reserves. They have also built a Merkle Tree system, so you can verify that your assets are included in their liability reports.

The exchange also operates with zero debt in its capital structure and maintains an emergency Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU) to cover extreme cases. Two‑factor authentication, address whitelisting, and cold‑storage wallets provide further safeguards against hacks. While no platform is risk‑free, Binance’s combination of transparency, insurance, and technical security obviously makes it a relatively safe choice for spot trading when used responsibly.

What Are Binance Spot Trading Supported and Restricted Countries?

The Binance spot trading supported countries are spread across Asia, Europe, Africa, Oceania, and parts of Latin America. Millions of people from India, the Philippines, Australia, Germany, France, Nigeria, Turkey, Brazil, Argentina, and many other jurisdictions trade on the platform daily. Hence, users from these countries can open accounts, complete verification, deposit fiat or crypto, and access the full range of spot pairs.

Binance spot trading access is restricted in some jurisdictions due to legal and regulatory concerns. Binance’s terms of use explicitly prohibit customers from the United States, Canada (Ontario), Iran, Cuba, the Crimea region, and North Korea. You may also face limitations if local regulators do not license Binance or if sanctions apply. People in the U.S. can only use the separate Binance.US platform, which lists fewer coins and has different fee structures.

Is Binance Spot Trading Available in the U.S.?

No, Binance.com spot trading is not available to customers residing in the United States because of regulatory restrictions. Hence, U.S. residents cannot open accounts on the global exchange or trade its full set of spot pairs. 

Instead, they must use Binance.US, an independent entity operated under U.S. regulatory frameworks. The American platform offers a smaller selection of coins and features compared with Binance.com, and fees and VIP tiers differ. It still provides market and limit orders, but some advanced products and promotions are not available. So, if you live in the United States, make sure you register with Binance.US and follow local Know‑Your‑Customer (KYC) and tax reporting rules.

What Are the Unique Key Features of Binance Spot Trading?

The unique features of Binance spot trading are unmatched liquidity across 1,500+ pairs, tiered fee discounts & BNB integration, seamless ecosystem with built-in earnings, and leading security with SAFU insurance.

Unmatched Liquidity Across 1,500+ Pairs

The depth of Binance’s order books is one of its standout strengths. You gain access to 500+ digital currencies and more than 1,500 spot trading pairs. This means you can trade everything from well‑known coins like BTC, ETH, and BNB to newer tokens in DeFi, gaming, and layer 2 ecosystems.

Liquidity remains robust even on mid‑cap pairs, and daily spot volume is over $10 billion, according to CMC data, which translates to tight bid‑ask spreads and rapid execution. High liquidity also allows you to enter or exit positions at almost any time. Unlike smaller exchanges, where a single trade might move the market, Binance’s depth absorbs orders smoothly.

Tiered Fee Discounts & BNB Integration

The Binance standard maker and taker fee is 0.1%. By holding BNB, the exchange’s native token, you can pay fees with BNB and receive a 25% discount. This reduces your effective rate to 0.075%, which beats many other centralized exchanges. Binance also provides 9 VIP levels. As your 30‑day trading volume increases and your BNB balance grows, you will qualify for lower fees. VIP 1 lowers maker fees to 0.09% and taker fees to 0.10%, while VIP 9 can bring maker fees down to 0.011% and taker fees to 0.023%.

The platform runs periodic promotions offering zero maker and taker fees on specific trading pairs. For example, BTC/FDUSD and ETH/FDUSD have seen zero‑fee periods. Beyond spot fees, Binance offers rebates for market makers, referral commissions if you bring friends to the platform, and additional savings through trading challenges.

Seamless Ecosystem & Built-In Earning

Spot trading on Binance is part of a larger ecosystem designed to make cryptocurrency useful in daily life. After you buy tokens, you can stake them on Binance Earn and earn interest through savings products, launchpools, or on-chain staking. You can earn APY as high as 20% on some of your top altcoins like DOT, ATOM, and more.

The exchange also operates Binance Pay, a payment network that lets you spend crypto at supported merchants or send funds to friends without fees. You can also order a Binance Card in some countries, which converts crypto to fiat when you pay, letting you spend digital assets like a debit card. All these features connect under one login, so you don’t need multiple accounts to trade, learn, and earn.

Leading Security & SAFU Insurance

Binance is a highly secure crypto exchange. The Proof‑of‑Reserves page shows that user assets are fully backed at least 1:1, with additional reserves. Also, corporate holdings are stored on a separate ledger, so user assets are not mixed. The proof‑of‑reserves system employs Merkle Tree and zk‑SNARK technologies, allowing you to verify that your balances are included in the report without revealing personal information.

The company has zero debt and an emergency Secure Asset Fund for Users (SAFU), an insurance pool funded by trading fees, that can cover losses in extreme cases. The exchange uses multi‑layer cold storage for the majority of funds and keeps only a small portion in hot wallets for withdrawals. Other features, like two‑factor authentication, address whitelisting, and cooldown periods for withdrawals, help prevent unauthorized access.

What Are the Binance Spot Trading Fees in 2025?

Binance charges spot traders a base fee of 0.1% for both makers and takers. Using BNB to pay fees lowers this rate to 0.075%, and as your trading volume increases, you can qualify for VIP tiers with reduced fees. 

Binance spot trading platform also has promotional zero‑fee trading on selected pairs like BTC/FDUSD. Crypto deposits are free, though network transaction fees apply when withdrawing tokens. Fiat deposits and withdrawals may involve bank or payment processor charges depending on your region.

To understand how the fees work, consider an example. Imagine you place a market order to buy 1,000 USDT worth of BTC. As a regular user with no VIP status and without using BNB, your taker fee would be 0.1%, so you pay 1 USDT in fees. If you hold enough BNB and choose to pay fees with it, the rate drops to 0.075%, so you pay 0.75 USDT instead.

How to Do Spot Trade on Binance: A Step-by-Step Guide

To spot trade on the Binance website, you need to log in, deposit funds, open the spot trading page, choose a pair, place your order, and confirm. To spot trade on the Binance app, you need to download the app, log in and complete KYC, deposit funds, access the market, select your trading pair, place a trade, and confirm.

How to Do Spot Trade on the Binance Website?

Step 1: Log In to Binance

You need to start by navigating to binance.com and logging in to your account with your email and password. Make sure you have completed the necessary identity verification because Binance requires KYC before enabling full trading. Also, if you don’t have a Binance account, you can use our Binance referral code during registration and get a $100 free crypto sign-up bonus.

Step 2: Deposit Funds

Once logged in, you have to locate the “Wallet” tab on the top menu and choose to deposit funds. You can either transfer crypto from another wallet or deposit fiat currency through a bank transfer or any other supported payment method.

Step 3: Open the Spot Trading Interface

Next, click “Trade” in the top menu and select Spot. Here, you will see the price chart, order book, and buy/sell form. You need to select your desired trading pair from the top left, such as BTC/USDT for trading Bitcoin against Tether.

Step 4: Place Your Trade

You have to decide which type of order suits your strategy. A Market order buys or sells instantly at the best available price, while a Limit order lets you set an exact entry or exit price. You need to enter the amount of the cryptocurrency for your buy and sell orders in the order form. 

Next, if you are buying, select the percentage of your USDT balance to spend; if you are selling, enter the amount of BTC to sell. Once you click Buy BTC or Sell BTC, the system processes your order and updates your balance. You can then view your completed orders and trade history in the Orders tab.

How to Do Spot Trade on the Binance App?

Step 1. Download the App and Log In

First, download the Binance app from the Google Play Store or Apple App Store and log in using your credentials. After completing KYC, tap Wallets at the bottom of the screen and choose to deposit funds. You can scan a QR code to transfer crypto, or use a bank card or payment service for fiat.

Step 2. Access the Market

Once funded, tap Trades on the home screen to access the market. Choose the pair you want by tapping the search bar and entering a symbol like “ETH/USDT.”

Step 3. Place and Confirm Your Trade

Select Buy or Sell and pick your order type – market, limit, or stop-limit. Enter the price and quantity, confirm the details, and slide to submit. The app shows a confirmation once the trade executes. You can check your positions and order history by navigating to Orders within the app. For more info about the exchange, you can check out our in-depth Binance review.

Tips for Safe and Successful Spot Trading on Binance

The tips for safe and successful spot trading on Binance are using strong security, doing research, setting risk limits, using fee discounts, and withdrawing to personal wallets for long-term storage.

  • Use strong security practices: Enable two‑factor authentication on your account, create a unique password, and use address whitelisting, so withdrawals only go to approved wallets. Also, try to avoid logging in on shared devices and update your credentials regularly.
  • Do your research: Spend time understanding the projects you trade. Read whitepapers, follow the news, and analyze price charts. By learning about market trends and fundamentals, you make better entry and exit decisions rather than acting on hype.
  • Set clear risk limits: Decide how much capital you are willing to risk on each trade and adhere to that limit. Use stop‑limit or OCO orders to cut losses if the market moves against you. Diversify across several assets instead of concentrating all funds in one coin.
  • Take advantage of fee discounts: Hold BNB in your account to pay trading fees at a discount, and aim to progress through VIP tiers if you trade large volumes. Watch for promotional zero‑fee pairs and use them when they align with your strategy.
  • Withdraw to personal wallets: While Binance is secure, keeping long‑term holdings in a private wallet reduces custodial risk. Only store the amount you need for active trades on the exchange. Regularly check that your withdrawals go through and verify wallet addresses carefully before confirming transactions.

title: CMC Markets Lets UK Clients Buy Options on Anthropic Before It Lists
summary:

Clients can buy calls and puts, and ...
content:
2026-11-14T20:49:58.558+02:00

Saturday, 14/11/2026 | 18:49 GMT by Damian Chmiel

  • Clients can buy calls and puts on a pre-IPO grey market, and the premium paid is the most they can lose.
  • CMC sets that grey price itself, from the expected listing price instead of trades in private shares.

CMC Markets has started selling UK clients options tied to Anthropic's expected share price before the artificial intelligence company lists, it said today (Saturday). CMC described itself as the first UK-regulated broker to offer options on pre-IPO grey markets.

Clients can buy calls and puts, and the premium paid is the most they can lose, according to CMC. The pre-IPO contracts other brokers opened on Anthropic in recent weeks are leveraged contracts for difference, priced two different ways at ThinkMarkets and Pepperstone.

Anthropic filed for a Nasdaq listing on October 26. Since then, the race to sell UK retail investors some form of exposure has drawn brokers, a crypto exchange and the company's own share offer.

London's trading industry is coming home!

How the Options Settle

The options are European-style and cash-settled. If Anthropic lists before an option expires, the contract settles against the official closing price of the listed shares, CMC said. If it has not listed, settlement uses the grey market price.

The product builds on the grey market spread bets and CFDs CMC first offered on SpaceX in May, which are leveraged and roll into ordinary share positions once a company trades. CMC clients traded an estimated $451 billion a month over the two quarters to September, FM Intelligence's broker volumes data show.

Laurence Booth, global head of markets at CMC Markets, presented the options as a way into companies that retail clients usually cannot reach before a listing.

"It significantly broadens the range of opportunities available," Booth said.

When it launched SpaceX trading, CMC had not said how it would set the grey market price. Its website now says CMC sets it from its own view of the expected listing price, using the indicative price range where one exists, valuations of comparable listed companies and market sentiment.

The price is not based on trades in private shares, and with no exchange-traded reference before a listing, the product cannot be hedged in the open market, according to the same page. Option prices add an estimate of future volatility on top.

What Each Route Gives a Retail Client

Brokers and exchanges now sell UK retail investors at least four kinds of exposure to the same listing, and they differ in what the client ends up holding.

ThinkMarkets quotes Anthropic's value at the end of its first trading day, while Pepperstone tracks the expected opening share price. Both are leveraged CFDs, the category in which European regulators have also placed perpetual futures.

Kraken lets eligible clients request share-backed ANTx tokens, The Defiant reported this week, with no allocation guaranteed. For the shares themselves, Anthropic has named six UK platforms for a retail offer coordinated by RetailBook, a list that does not include Robinhood.

Of the four, the share offer and the tokens give the client a claim on stock. CMC's options are the only one of the derivatives where the maximum loss is known when the trade opens.

CMC said the options are available to UK clients from Saturday, with a broader global rollout planned. Clients must pass an appropriateness assessment for both OTC options and grey market products, according to its website.
