title: Google Launches Gemini 4 Hydrogen With 2.5x Faster Performance, Challenging GPT-6.1 and Claude
summary: Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more efficient AI model designed to compete with frontier systems while expanding its presence across search, coding, and agentic workflows.
content:
Skip to content

Google has introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen, a faster and more efficient AI model designed to compete with frontier systems while expanding its presence across search, coding, and agentic workflows.

Announced on November 12, the model brings a reported 2.5x improvement in task completion speed over Gemini 3.8 Flash, alongside stronger coding capabilities and lower execution costs. Google is positioning Hydrogen as an accessible option for developers and businesses that need fast AI execution without relying on its more computationally intensive models.

Google announced the global rollout of Gemini 4 Hydrogen, upgrading Search’s intent recognition to better understand complex, nuanced queries, including typos and natural language. Source: Google via X

The release also marks a significant expansion of Google’s Gemini 4 ecosystem, with the model becoming available across Google Search, the Gemini app, AI Studio, and developer platforms. Its benchmark results place it ahead of GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in several categories, although competitors retain advantages in other specialized tasks.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Targets Faster AI Coding and Agentic Workflows

Google DeepMind designed Gemini 4 Hydrogen to handle everyday coding, software development, multimodal tasks, and agentic workflows with greater execution speed. Unlike Gemini 4 Carbon and Gemini 4 Argon, which focus on complex reasoning and longer tasks, Hydrogen prioritizes rapid execution and efficiency.

Google introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a fast, efficient model for everyday coding, agentic workflows, and rapid execution, complementing Gemini 4 Carbon’s advanced reasoning capabilities. Source: Google AI via X

According to Google, Hydrogen completes tasks 2.5 times faster than Gemini 3.8 Flash at its default high thinking setting. The company also reported that its Terminal-Bench 4.1 score increased to 57%, compared with 18.2% for its predecessor.

The improvement extends beyond processing speed. Google said Hydrogen reduces fabricated claims by more than five times and handles unsuccessful tool calls or empty search results more effectively. These capabilities are particularly relevant to autonomous AI agents, which must navigate multiple steps, use external tools, and recover from errors without constant human intervention.

The model also introduces four configurable thinking levels, including a new xhigh setting. Users can adjust the reasoning effort according to the complexity of their tasks, balancing response speed against the resources required for more demanding work.

Google DeepMind said Hydrogen also surpassed Gemini 4 Argon on the Artificial Intelligence Index at its default high setting, scoring 51 against Argon’s 50. Its score rises to 54 when using the highest xhigh setting.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Challenges GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5

Google’s published benchmark evaluations show that Gemini 4 Hydrogen can compete with established frontier models across coding, reasoning, and professional workflows.

In the SWE-sweep evaluation, which measures an AI model’s ability to identify and repair software issues, Hydrogen scored 13.5%. This exceeded Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 3.1% and GPT-6.1 Terra at 5.8%.

Google DeepMind introduced Gemini 4 Hydrogen as a faster upgrade over Gemini 3.8 Flash, optimized for coding, multimodal tasks, agentic workflows, and everyday use. Source: @GoogleDeepMind via X

Hydrogen also recorded a 71.6% score on Agents’ Last Exam v1.1, ahead of GPT-6.1 Terra at 69.8% and Claude Sonnet 5.5 at 60.4%. The benchmark evaluates how effectively AI systems complete complex professional tasks involving multiple steps and different forms of information.

Its HLE-Diamond score reached 58.8%, compared with 53.3% for Claude Sonnet 5.5 and 47.3% for GPT-6.1 Terra. On AutomationBench-AA, Hydrogen achieved 76.1%, outperforming both competitors in the published comparison.

However, the results do not establish an across-the-board advantage. Claude Sonnet 5.5 scored 63.9% on Terminal-Bench 4.1, above Hydrogen’s 57%. Claude also led the OSWorld-2.1 computer-use evaluation with 83.9%, compared with Hydrogen’s 77.6%.

Google’s evaluation methodology combines its own testing with results reported by competing model providers and public benchmark leaderboards. The company also used different testing configurations across evaluations, making individual benchmark results more useful than treating the overall comparison as a definitive ranking.

Nevertheless, the results demonstrate Google’s progress in making a faster model competitive across several demanding AI applications.

Independent Tests Highlight Gemini 4 Hydrogen’s Cost Advantage

Early demonstrations from independent developers have also drawn attention to Hydrogen’s execution speed and operating costs.

In one comparison shared by developer @EnvolDev, Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Gemini 4 Carbon were assigned the same complex task through OpenRouter using the High setting. Hydrogen completed the task in 1 hour and 23 minutes at a reported cost of $4.27.

A split-screen video compares Gemini 4 Hydrogen and Carbon generating an arctic boat scene, highlighting Hydrogen’s faster execution and lower cost. Source: @EnvolDev/X

Gemini 4 Carbon took 2 hours and 39 minutes and cost $8.83 to complete the same task. The side-by-side demonstration showed both models generating an arctic boat scene with ice formations and marine elements.

Although this was an individual test rather than a standardized benchmark, the results highlight the potential cost and time advantages of using Hydrogen for workloads that do not require the deeper reasoning capabilities of Carbon.

A separate demonstration shared by @AI_Screening compared Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Carbon, and Argon in AI video generation. The models generated a stylized horse galloping across a savanna at sunset, allowing viewers to compare motion quality, environmental effects, and visual consistency.

Hydrogen delivered competitive animation quality in the demonstration while offering faster generation and lower costs. These results suggest that the model could provide an efficient option for certain multimodal creative workflows, although individual demonstrations do not establish consistent performance across different prompts and generation tasks.

Google Upgrades Search With Gemini 4 Hydrogen

Alongside the model launch, Google has introduced a significant upgrade to Google Search, integrating Gemini 4 Hydrogen to improve how the platform understands and responds to complicated queries.

The November 12 rollout allows Search to interpret more nuanced, multi-part questions, including requests written in natural language or containing difficult-to-understand typos. The system is designed to identify the user’s intent more accurately rather than relying solely on individual keywords.

Google has also improved its query fan-out capabilities. The technology allows Search to explore several related subtopics simultaneously, connecting users with a wider selection of relevant websites and information sources.

The updated experience introduces more adaptive visual responses, including images, comparison tables, structured information, and custom tools. These features are intended to make complicated searches easier to understand without requiring users to navigate multiple pages manually.

Robby Stein, Google’s vice president of product for Search, described the release as the biggest model upgrade to Search yet. He said the update would help users find relevant information through more intuitive and visually structured responses.

Google also highlighted improvements to language understanding across supported AI Mode languages, extending the upgraded search experience to users making queries in different languages.

The integration is particularly important for Google’s broader AI strategy because it brings Gemini’s reasoning and information-processing capabilities directly into one of the company’s most widely used products.

Gemini 4 Hydrogen Expands Across Google’s AI Ecosystem

Google is making Gemini 4 Hydrogen available across its consumer, developer, and enterprise platforms, increasing access to its latest AI capabilities.

Developers can use the model through the Gemini API, Google AI Studio, and Android Studio. Businesses can also access it through Gemini for business and supported enterprise tools, while general users can find Hydrogen in the Gemini app and Google Search.

A split-screen comparison evaluates Gemini 4 Hydrogen, Carbon (Medium), and Argon in generating a galloping horse scene, highlighting differences in motion quality, dust effects, and visual consistency. Source: @AI_Screening/X

Google is also introducing a multi-model approach through its Antigravity development platform. Its Orchestrator feature can dynamically switch between Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen during a single session, assigning more complex reasoning tasks to Carbon and faster execution work to Hydrogen.

According to Google, this approach achieved near-Carbon task success rates on Terminal-Bench 4.0 while using 24% less quota and completing tasks 19% faster on average.

The model’s API pricing is set at $1.50 per million input tokens and $7.50 per million output tokens across its one-million-token context window. This gives developers a defined cost structure when integrating Hydrogen into applications and automated workflows.

By combining configurable reasoning, faster execution, and multi-model coordination, Google is targeting users who need to manage increasingly complex AI workloads without relying exclusively on its most resource-intensive systems.

Google’s AI Competition Intensifies

The launch of Gemini 4 Hydrogen strengthens Google’s position in an increasingly competitive AI market, where model performance is no longer measured solely by reasoning capabilities.

Speed, inference costs, coding accuracy, and the ability to complete multi-step tasks have become important factors for developers and businesses choosing AI systems. Google’s latest release addresses these requirements while extending its Gemini technology into Search and everyday productivity tools.

Its benchmark performance against GPT-6.1 Terra and Claude Sonnet 5.5 provides evidence of progress in several categories, although differences in computer use and terminal-based tasks show that competitors remain competitive.

The introduction of Hydrogen also reflects a broader shift toward specialized AI models that can handle routine execution more efficiently while working alongside larger systems for demanding reasoning tasks.

As Google expands access to Gemini 4 Hydrogen, its ability to maintain benchmark performance while delivering measurable savings in execution time and costs will be an important factor in determining its adoption among developers, enterprises, and everyday users.

title: AI Agents Can Now Buy Computing With Bitcoin—Does Lightning Have Its Use Case?
summary: Lightning Labs’ pi402 lets coding agents pay for AI inference with Bitcoin. The launch tests whether tiny automated payments can solve a real computing business problem.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: BTC

Lightning Labs’ pi402 lets coding agents pay for AI inference with Bitcoin. The launch tests whether tiny automated payments can solve a real computing business problem.

AI agents have a new way to spend Bitcoin: buying the computing needed to keep working. Lightning Labs has launched pi402, a tool that lets coding agents pay for AI inference over the Lightning Network.

The November 12 announcement moves the agent-payments debate toward a specific purchase. Rather than imagining software shopping autonomously for everything, it starts with a recurring need: access to an AI model that can process the next prompt.

“Inference is the fuel every agent runs on,” Lightning Labs’ Olaoluwa Osuntokun wrote. The business question is whether a Bitcoin payment can make that fuel easier to buy and sell.

How AI agents use Bitcoin for inference

Pi402 connects the Pi coding-agent environment with paid inference services. The launch describes an embedded Wavelength wallet and controls for per-request spending and daily budgets. A human still funds the wallet and sets the operating boundaries.

The attraction is access without creating a separate buyer account or supplying a card to each participating seller. That does not make the entire AI service anonymous, unregulated or free of provider conditions. It changes the payment and access mechanism for services that implement it.

According to the L402 documentation, a buyer first requests a protected resource. The server returns a payment-required response, a credential and a Lightning invoice. Paying produces proof that can be presented with the credential to gain access.

The payment becomes part of authorisation rather than an invoice to settle later. The documentation also describes restricting and delegating bearer credentials, which matters when one piece of software needs to give another a limited ability to buy or access resources.

The useful detail is metering, not a payment for every word

The Aperture v0.6.0 release notes describe prepaid bundles that are drawn down according to actual usage. A single Lightning payment can therefore support multiple model requests. The system does not need to initiate a separate payment for every generated token.

The proxy obtains a price, reserves an estimated amount for a request and accounts for the reported usage afterward. When the remaining balance cannot cover another request, it can issue a new payment challenge.

That distinction separates a plausible billing system from a flashy demonstration. Model responses vary in length. Sellers need a way to price that uncertainty, and buyers need to see what they have actually consumed.

The same release supports both L402 and the Payment HTTP Authentication Scheme used by the Machine Payments Protocol. Supporting more than one payment-authentication format could help services meet different clients, although compatibility by itself does not establish commercial adoption.

The seller still has costs, accounts and exchange-rate exposure

Lightning Labs’ public Lightmeter repository shows another important layer. It converts a provider’s dollar-denominated model prices into millisatoshis per token, can add a seller margin and reconciles usage against the provider’s billing records.

A millisatoshi is one-thousandth of a satoshi. That granularity allows small accounting units, but the conversion does not make the underlying computing free or ensure that Bitcoin-denominated prices stay constant.

The repository’s architecture places the upstream provider’s API key at the proxy. In other words, removing an API key from the buyer’s experience does not necessarily remove API keys from the supply chain. Someone still needs to secure the provider relationship and pay its bill.

That gives the story a more grounded commercial angle. A reseller could offer a narrow, paid entry point to computing while managing procurement and billing behind it. Whether that arrangement is attractive depends on price, reliability, model access and the terms of the upstream service.

Why irreversible payments are a trade-off

Osuntokun argues that card chargebacks are poorly matched to computing that has already been consumed. A completed response cannot be ungenerated so that a seller can recover the electricity and GPU time.

Final payment can reduce that particular uncertainty for a seller. For a buyer, however, it raises the importance of spending controls and service quality. Paying successfully establishes access; it does not prove that an answer is correct or that an autonomous workflow was worth its cost.

BNC’s coverage of Claude Fable and Mythos 5.2 examined falling model prices alongside the continuing need for human judgment. Automating payment makes that distinction more consequential: a system can spend efficiently while pursuing an unhelpful task.

The adoption test starts with something measurable

The launch supplies software and an identifiable use case, rather than evidence that a large new market already exists. The announcement does not establish independent transaction volume, recurring demand or a broad network of competing sellers.

Useful follow-up evidence would include repeat purchases, the number of active providers, total payment costs and how often spending limits prevent unwanted work. Those measures would help distinguish a convenient developer tool from a meaningful new source of Lightning usage.

For Bitcoin, the opportunity is straightforward: a machine-native service being bought through a machine-readable payment. Pi402 makes that proposition testable. Its success will depend on whether developers keep choosing it after the novelty of an agent with a wallet has worn off.

title: Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low
Bitcoin price crashed about 13% over the past week and traded near $65,600 on Saturday.
This post Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low first appeared o...
content:
Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike.

A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning.

A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900.

Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough.

A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price

The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes.

Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. Traders fully priced a quarter-point hike at the Fed’s Dec. 8-9 meeting, CME FedWatch data show.

Chip stocks offered no cushion. The iShares Semiconductor ETF fell more than 3% on Friday, and Advanced Micro Devices dropped more than 8%. The Nasdaq 100 closed down 1.22%. U.S. stock and bond markets are closed Saturday, but those levels still frame the weekend session. Nvidia is due to report third-quarter results on Tuesday under interim CEO Colette Kress, the first earnings release since Huang stepped down.

ETF outflows continue as mining difficulty drops

Demand from spot bitcoin ETFs has not filled the gap. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) bled $2 billion over nine straight days of outflows through Wednesday, and the funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday. Weekend trading is typically thinner, leaving the bitcoin price more exposed to sharp swings in either direction.

Miners got some relief overnight. Bitcoin’s mining difficulty dropped 9.13% at 12:02 a.m. ET Saturday at block 975,744, falling from about 148.36 trillion to 134.82 trillion, the largest cut since June. Difficulty adjusts automatically every 2,016 blocks to keep average block times near 10 minutes.

The next tests for the bitcoin price arrive quickly. title: MSCI Cuts Strategy From Global Indexes, Putting Bitcoin Treasury Model Under Pressure
summary:
Key Takeaways: Under new classification rules instituted by MSCI, Strategy will be phased out of the global equity index. The changes come into effect following the Nov. 30 sell call
The post MSCI Cuts Strategy From Global Indexes, Putting Bitcoin Treasury Model Under Pressure appeared first on Cryp...
content:
Key Takeaways:

  • Under new classification rules instituted by MSCI, Strategy will be phased out of the global equity index.
  • The changes come into effect following the Nov. 30 sell call time, which could push index-tracking funds to sell MSTR shares.
  • Strategy challenges MSCI’s methodology, states funds connected to MSCI indexes only cover 3.1% of underlying stocks.

Major index provider MSCI has made a roundup of its corporate Bitcoin holdings, with Strategy going down from its list of big names. The ruling would impair passive demand for MSTR as well as a fresh hurdle for the digital asset treasury system championed by Michael Saylor’s firm.

  • Strategy Gets Cut Under MSCI’s New Eligibility Rules
  • Passive Funds Could Be Forced to Sell MSTR
    • Strategy Rejects the “Non-Operating” Label

Strategy Gets Cut Under MSCI’s New Eligibility Rules

MSCI confirmed in its November 2026 Index Review that changes across its equity benchmarks will be implemented at the close of trading on Nov. 30 and become effective Dec. 1.

The change comes after MSCI decided in October to exclude some “non-operating companies” from its Global Investable Market Indexes. The framework is designed for corporate issues showing features of an investment fund or passive investment vehicle.

Strategy, along with several other firms such as Metaplanet, is slated for removal after MSCI determined the companies’ structures are more akin to an investment vehicle than to standard operating companies, Reuters wrote.

Read More: Poolin, Once a Dominant Bitcoin Mining Giant, Announces Bankruptcy

Passive Funds Could Be Forced to Sell MSTR

The reason index exclusion plays a role is because most passive funds tracking the MSCI indexes tend to rebalance their holdings when there are additions and deletions. That will essentially cause Strategy to sell-off automatically from any funds that may hold the ticker MSTR just due to the fact that it’s in the index.

In its previous assessment, JPMorgan said that dropping out of the index could cost around $2.8 billion in selling, since the effect could be greater should other big index providers follow suit.

Following the decision, strategy shares of the stocks tumbled in extended trading adding more stress on a stock already closely correlated with Bitcoin’s performance.

Strategy Rejects the “Non-Operating” Label

The Strategy response, which highlights MSCI’s framework, is very critical. The company says there is no defined basis in U.S. GAAP, IFRS or existing securities law for the terminology and it also asserts that the method is quite a form of the previous proposal especially to digital asset treasury companies.

In addition, strategy reports its Bitcoin business on U.S. GAAP as an operating segment.

Meanwhile, the company has been downplaying its magnitude of direct exposure to MSCI. In total, it estimates that there are some 13 million MSTR shares held by MSCI Global Investable Market Index (IMI) linked funds which account for around 3.1% of the registered number of basic shares on issue and less than a day of total trades.

The dispute now reaches beyond Strategy itself. MSCI’s move sets a precedent for how many traditional stock indexes will handle companies whose balance sheets are largely composed of Bitcoin or other digital assets.

title: XRP Price Today: $0.98 Support Under Threat Despite Oversold RSI
summary: XRP fell below the $1 psychological threshold on November 14, trading near $0.98 as persistent selling pressure pushed the cryptocurrency to multi-month lows.
content:
Skip to content
Assets: XRP

XRP fell below the $1 psychological threshold on November 14, trading near $0.98 as persistent selling pressure pushed the cryptocurrency to multi-month lows.

Deeply oversold indicators suggest a possible relief bounce, but the broader technical structure remains bearish.

The XRP price has declined approximately 4% over 24 hours, 15% over the past week, and more than 25% over the past month. The latest correction has placed the $0.98–$0.99 region under pressure, raising concerns about whether buyers can prevent another move toward $0.80.

Bears Test $0.98–$0.99 Critical Support

XRP was trading between approximately $0.982 and $0.986 on November 14, following a decline that briefly pushed the asset below $1. The weakness reflects broader pressure across the cryptocurrency market, alongside a deterioration in XRP’s technical structure.

XRP failed to break $1.55 resistance, reversing from recent highs toward the channel’s lower boundary near $0.99. Source: Ali Martinez/X

In a three-day chart analysis, crypto analyst Ali Charts identified approximately $0.99 as the lower boundary of an established trading channel. XRP had previously failed to overcome resistance near $1.55 before reversing toward this level.

The analyst warned that losing $0.99 could expose the cryptocurrency to further losses toward $0.80. For an initial recovery, XRP needs to reclaim $1 and move above the $1.02 pivot region, with immediate resistance around $1.04 and $1.06.

XRP Technical Indicators Signal Strong Selling Pressure

XRP’s moving averages continue to reflect a strong bearish trend. Multi-timeframe readings show the cryptocurrency trading below its short-, medium-, and long-term simple and exponential moving averages.

XRP price chart. Source: Brave New Coin

The 10-period averages are positioned around $1.08–$1.09, while the 20-period readings sit near $1.16–$1.18. Longer-term averages are considerably higher, with the 50-period indicators around $1.26–$1.32 and the 200-period readings near $1.26–$1.34.

This positioning highlights the distance XRP must recover before challenging its previous trading levels.

The Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) remains negative near -0.08, with its signal line around -0.06. Its negative histogram indicates that bearish momentum has not yet produced a confirmed reversal. The Average Directional Index (ADX) also points to a relatively strong directional trend on several timeframes.

Together, these readings show that the prevailing downtrend remains established, despite signs of extreme selling conditions in shorter-term oscillators.

Oversold RSI Raises the Possibility of an XRP Rebound

The daily Relative Strength Index (RSI) is hovering around 19.8–20.8, considerably below the conventional 30 threshold for oversold conditions. Other oscillators show similar extremes, with Stochastic %K near 3–5, the Commodity Channel Index (CCI) around -130 to -143, and Williams %R near -98 to -99.

These readings indicate that XRP has experienced intense selling pressure. They also raise the possibility of short-term consolidation or a technical rebound if buyers begin entering the market.

However, oversold conditions do not guarantee a price recovery. An asset can remain in this territory during an extended downtrend, particularly when broader market sentiment remains weak.

A sustained recovery above the $1.02 pivot, accompanied by improving momentum, would provide more convincing evidence that selling pressure is easing. Until then, the RSI readings alone are insufficient to establish a bullish reversal.

Coinbase XRP Buying Activity Offers a Contrasting Signal

Despite the broader decline, exchange-flow data has revealed a potentially important development in XRP’s market structure.

Crypto analyst CW8900 reported that Coinbase shifted to net XRP buying over two consecutive days after recording substantial initial selling activity that coincided with the recent price decline.

The volume of net selling on Coinbase was significantly higher than that seen on Binance or OKX during the decline. Source: @CW8900/X

The analyst’s exchange-flow comparison examined price movements, trading volume, and cumulative netflow or delta readings across Coinbase, Binance, Bitfinex, and OKX.

The data highlighted significant volatility around November 13, when selling pressure and leveraged liquidations contributed to XRP’s downward movement.

Coinbase’s subsequent shift toward net buying is notable because the exchange had previously recorded comparatively heavy net selling. The change suggests that buying activity emerged even as XRP remained under pressure.

The analyst also highlighted whale activity and high-leverage liquidations during the decline. The resulting accumulation signals indicate that some market participants were willing to acquire XRP at lower prices despite the market’s weakness.

However, net buying on a single exchange does not establish that the broader market has entered an accumulation phase. It also does not confirm that XRP has reached a price bottom.

Nevertheless, the development offers a contrasting perspective to the bearish technical indicators and suggests that buying interest has not disappeared entirely.

XRP Price Prediction: $0.75 Support and $10 Long-Term Projection

A separate monthly XRP chart analysis identifies a broader ascending channel that could influence the cryptocurrency’s longer-term direction.

According to the analysis, the price remains within a rising channel, with its lower trendline serving as an important structural support. The $0.75 region is highlighted as a critical level for preserving this formation.

XRP maintains a broader ascending channel, with $0.75 serving as critical support for preserving its bullish structure; a breakdown could trigger a deeper correction. Source: TradingView

A sustained hold above $0.75 would keep the ascending-channel structure intact, while a confirmed breakdown could indicate a deeper correction and deteriorating long-term sentiment.

The monthly RSI currently stands near 41, below its neutral midpoint of 50. This indicates weakening momentum, although it does not represent the extreme oversold conditions observed on the daily timeframe. A recovery above 50 would suggest improving longer-term buying momentum.

The analyst also outlined a potential long-term upside projection toward $10, based on the channel’s upper boundary. However, this remains a technical scenario rather than a confirmed price target. XRP would first need to stabilize, overcome intermediate resistance levels, and demonstrate sustained momentum improvement.

For now, the market presents conflicting signals. Bearish trend indicators point to continued pressure, while deeply oversold oscillators and Coinbase’s recent buying activity suggest that a short-term recovery remains possible. The coming price action will help determine whether XRP can stabilize or extend its correction.

content:
The futures prop trading sector faced renewed questions over its business model, with exchange data costs and low-priced challenges putting pressure on firms operating without recurring subscriptions. Meanwhile, established industry figures returned with new businesses, while brokers continued to expand their regulatory and corporate structures.

London's trading industry is coming home!

The week also brought developments in brokerage technology, corporate governance and retail trading activity. IG Group advanced its planned move to Jersey, CFI secured preliminary approval for a crypto brokerage operation in Dubai, and eToro reported weaker crypto trading activity despite account growth.

Artificial intelligence, prediction markets and technology disruptions also featured among the week’s developments.

Futures Prop Firms Face Rising CME Data Costs Under One-Time Pricing Models

Several futures proprietary trading firms have moved away from monthly subscriptions towards one-time challenge fees, raising questions about the sustainability of their pricing models. Apex, Tradeify, Bulenox and My Funded Futures made the shift in 2026, while exchange data costs continue to recur monthly for active users.

CME’s real-time annual licence fee is $29,280 per exchange, although many firms access data through platform vendors rather than licensing it directly. TradersYard’s co-founder Manuel Sonnleithner said a prop-specific simulation licence requires all four exchanges, bringing the base fee to $117,120 annually, before additional monthly data charges.

The mismatch between recurring operating costs and one-off customer payments remains a central challenge.

Futures Prop Firms See Margins Squeezed by $49 Challenges and Rising Costs

The pressure on futures prop firms extends beyond exchange data fees, with lower challenge prices and higher operating costs reducing profitability. TradersYard CEO Manuel Sonnleithner, citing internal industry data, estimated that net margins have fallen from 25-30% to 10-15%. Platform expenses, including monthly charges per user, make low-priced challenges harder to sustain.

Ruben Abitbol of RUBIK said futures firms generally face higher operating costs than CFD prop firms, partly because of platform and market-data expenses. Payout ratios also differ, with futures firms typically paying out 70-80% compared with 40-50% for CFD firms, according to Abitbol’s broad benchmark.

Several operators, including FundingTicks, Rev One and FundedSeat, closed during 2026, and Alpha closed its Premium Plan.

Former iS Prime Founders Launch New Liquidity Business for Brokers

Three former iS Prime executives have launched JT Prime, a prime-of-prime liquidity provider targeting brokers, funds, family offices and proprietary trading firms.

Raj Sitlani and Jonathan Brewer, who co-founded iS Prime in 2014, established the business alongside Jeff Wilkins, who previously led iS Prime’s risk analytics operation.

JT Prime will offer aggregated Tier 1 bank and non-bank liquidity across foreign exchange, precious metals and index CFDs, with FIX API connectivity.

The business operates as the institutional arm of retail broker JT Markets. JT Markets currently holds a Seychelles licence, while an application in an unnamed Western market remains pending. The founders also plan to expand into digital assets.

CFI Receives Preliminary VARA Approval for Dubai Crypto Brokerage

CFI Financial Group has received in-principle approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority, known as VARA, for its crypto brokerage subsidiary, CFIX. The approval covers broker-dealer services, but the company cannot begin offering virtual asset services until it receives a full licence.

According to CFI, VARA requires the subsidiary to finalise its leadership appointments, operational infrastructure, governance arrangements and regulatory controls before granting final authorisation. CFI said CFIX would operate as a separate legal entity with its own governance structure.

The development adds another regulatory step to the group’s international expansion. CFI also holds authorisations in several jurisdictions, including Brazil, where it received approval for a securities brokerage earlier this year.

IG Group Advances Jersey Redomiciliation Ahead of November Listing Switch

IG Group secured court approval for its proposed move from England and Wales to Jersey, bringing the restructuring closer to completion. The transition will establish a new Jersey-incorporated holding company, Jenkins Topco, which will be renamed IG Group Holdings.

The move is scheduled to take effect on 13 November, subject to delivery of the court order to the Registrar of Companies. Existing shares will be cancelled, with new shares issued through the Jersey entity.

The current shares are scheduled to be delisted from the London Stock Exchange on 16 November, when the new shares are expected to begin trading. The group expects restructuring costs of £30 million in 2026.

CFI Chairman Says Independent Board Must Challenge Management Decisions

CFI Financial Group’s independent chairman, Federico Cirulli, outlined how the board oversees management as the broker expands its operations and regulatory footprint. Cirulli said independent directors should pressure-test management proposals rather than routinely block decisions.

The board sets strategic direction, establishes risk appetite and holds executives accountable, while Chief Executive Ziad Melhem manages daily operations. Cirulli also said founder-led structures are effective in the early stages, but that more stakeholders, a more complex offering and heavier regulation can call for a different structure.

CFI reported $3.45 trillion in trading volume during the third quarter, up 123% year-on-year, while nine-month volume reached $8.8 trillion, figures that are company-reported. Cirulli said governance and internal controls must keep pace with that expansion.

eToro Reports 62% Drop in Crypto Trades Despite Funded Account Growth

eToro’s clients placed 2 million cryptocurrency trades in October, down 62% from a year earlier, despite an 18% increase in funded accounts to 4.42 million. The average amount invested per crypto trade fell 29% to $228.

The figures followed a weaker third quarter, when net income dropped 74% year-on-year to $15 million and net contribution declined 13% to $186 million. Adjusted EBITDA fell 56% to $34.2 million.

Net trading income from equities, commodities and currencies increased 21% to $88.5 million, although it declined from the previous quarter. Chief Financial Officer Meron Shani said crypto activity had recovered sequentially compared with the second quarter.

eToro Targets $100 Million Latin American Revenue After Argentine Acquisition

eToro plans to generate $100 million in Latin American revenue within two to three years, using its proposed acquisition of Argentine fintech LB Finanzas as a regional base. The company agreed to acquire the investing and payments app for less than $20 million.

Chief Executive Yoni Assia gave analysts the target, and the article noted that eToro already has a larger online audience in the region than most retail brokers, according to FM Intelligence data.

The acquisition marks the company’s fourth deal announced in 2026, following purchases involving Zengo and Bit2C and an agreement to acquire US broker TradeZero. Assia said eToro would slow its acquisition activity to focus on integrating the businesses.

AI Trading Agents Create New Monitoring Challenges for Forex Brokers

Artificial intelligence agents are increasingly able to interact directly with retail trading accounts, creating new monitoring challenges for forex and CFD brokers, according to an op-ed by Marios Kyriakou, Head of FX Dealer Academy by Your Bourse.

Connections through platforms such as MetaTrader and cTrader allow AI tools to access trading functions through Model Context Protocol, or MCP, servers. These integrations can make it difficult for dealing desks to distinguish automated orders from trades placed manually by clients.

Remote setups may also involve access tokens held by third-party AI tools, limiting brokers’ visibility. While some official integrations offer read-only access and approval requirements before trades are executed, open-source and custom-built alternatives may lack similar safeguards. The development raises questions about client profiling, exposure management and operational risk.

AI Voice Agents Raise Questions About Client Trust in Forex Brokerage

Forex brokers are increasingly considering AI voice agents to handle customer acquisition and routine communications. The technology can contact prospective clients, chase account-opening documents through a secure upload link, follow up on incomplete applications and schedule calls with human representatives.

However, its use in client-facing conversations raises concerns about mis-selling and the boundaries of automated communication. Anish Lal, Chief Business Development Officer at BlackBull Markets, argued that voice agents should support administrative tasks rather than provide trading advice or encourage additional deposits, and that documents and card details should never be taken over the phone.

He also highlighted the importance of transparency, including informing customers when they are speaking to AI. Brokers must balance efficiency gains with appropriate controls and maintain human involvement where financial decisions and client trust are concerned.

Prediction Markets Seek Broker Partnerships to Sustain Trading Activity

Prediction market operators are increasingly turning to brokerage partnerships and wider product offerings to attract customers beyond major sporting and political events, according to a column by Paul Golden. The World Cup generated a significant increase in activity, but platforms now face the challenge of maintaining user engagement between major events.

Women are less than 25% of the user base on prediction markets like Kalshi and Polymarket… but are the largest consumers on Instagram and Facebook. I think Meta’s prediction market product will actually be a huge hit due to this untapped audience and the social/cultural topics they are interested in. Count me in for predicting who gets voted out next on Love Island. 🏝️

— Brit Morin 🦞 (@brit) July 7, 2026

Kalshi has expanded its distribution through partnerships with Alpaca and Public, allowing event contracts to reach customers through existing brokerage platforms. It has also introduced products beyond conventional event contracts, including a stock index perpetual future.

The expansion brings prediction markets closer to traditional financial products. However, regulatory uncertainty, particularly around sports-related contracts in the US, remains a challenge for operators seeking broader distribution.

Nvidia Shares Fall More Than 6% Following Jensen Huang’s Resignation

Nvidia shares fell more than 6% in trading after the announcement that co-founder Jensen Huang had resigned as president, chief executive and board member after 33 years leading the company, although the sell-off had begun before the announcement.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress has taken over as interim CEO while retaining her CFO responsibilities, and the board is considering internal and external candidates for a permanent successor. Former Synopsys chief executive Harvey Jones was appointed as Nvidia’s first board chairman.

The company did not state a reason for the departure, which followed an independent investigation announced by the board, which appointed former acting US Attorney Joon Kim and law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct the review. Jones said operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap would continue without interruption.

We're investigating reports of users experiencing issues accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods in the Americas. More details can be found in the Microsoft 365 admin center under EX1550543.

— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) November 12, 2026

Microsoft 365 Outage Disrupts Financial Markets and Broker Operations

A global Microsoft 365 outage disrupted financial firms across several markets, forcing trading desks and brokerages to rely on manual workarounds. The disruption, which had lasted 12 hours at the time of reporting, affected Exchange Online, with Downdetector recording more than 130,000 reports in the US at its peak.

Brokerages in Singapore and India reported delays in customer support, while CMC Markets in Singapore used phone calls and WhatsApp to bypass affected systems. Japanese financial firms also turned to manual processes as email authentication failures disrupted trade confirmations and settlements, and a Kalshi post joked that Japanese markets had switched to fax machines.

The outage highlighted the industry’s dependence on cloud-based services, with retail FX brokers also reporting difficulties involving customer logins and operational processes.

title: Your Broker's Growth is Elsewhere, ahead of 2027
summary:
Established acquisition markets are crowded, client acquisition costs are rising and brokerage product offerings often look remarkably alike. For firms planning growth in 2027, the more useful question is which new markets, products and partnerships have actually delivered results.
xecutives from ac...
content:
2026-11-14T08:00:00.000+02:00

Saturday, 14/11/2026 | 06:00 GMT by FM Events

  • Examine where brokers can find sustainable growth as acquisition costs rise and established markets become more competitive.

Established acquisition markets are crowded, client acquisition costs are rising and brokerage product offerings often look remarkably alike. For firms planning growth in 2027, the more useful question is which new markets, products and partnerships have actually delivered results.

xecutives from across the industry gathered at the Finance Magnates Summit London 2026 aim to examine growth strategies they have tested, from product diversification to regional expansion and partnerships.

Growth in retail brokerage is becoming harder to secure through familiar acquisition channels alone. Competition in established markets, rising acquisition costs and increasingly similar product propositions mean that commercial teams must be more selective about where they invest. The session will focus on strategies that firms have tested rather than forecasts that sound attractive on paper.

Speakers will consider where new products and assets have generated demand, how automation influences the client journey and which regional or partner channels remain commercially viable. They will also examine the costs behind expansion: setting up entities, meeting operational requirements and supporting customers after the first conversion.

The session is relevant to leaders responsible for acquisition, product, partnerships and profitability. A promising market is only valuable if a business can enter it sustainably, and a new feature matters only if it improves client outcomes or commercial performance. The aim is to help delegates frame sharper questions about their own growth plans for 2027.

Attend the session at 11:30 - 12:10 on 24 November and explore what the rest of the agenda has to offer: https://events.financemagnates.com/events/fmsummitlondon/agenda/schedule

Growth decisions increasingly require brokers to consider the entire client relationship rather than acquisition alone. Product relevance, onboarding, retention and regional execution all affect whether a promising opportunity becomes a sustainable business.

Delegates can use the discussion as a basis for conversations with technology, payments and brokerage specialists exhibiting at Old Billingsgate.

With 10 days to the summit, now is the time to secure your place:

title: Inside Prediction Markets: Kalshi Eyes $65B Valuation in the Shadow of State Bans
summary:
The prediction-market sector is manoeuvring between an escalating legal war of attrition and commercial euphoria. 
While state courts pushed their enforcement perimeter beyond retail apps and straight into clearing, platforms continued to print record volume with the CFTC playing the surreal dual ro...
content:
2026-11-13T23:14:00.000+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 21:14 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • State pushback escalated as a Louisiana court ordered 10 operators to halt trading, brokering, and clearing.
  • Nine platforms processed $30.4 billion in weekly notional volume, as Kalshi weighed fresh funding at $65 billion.

The prediction-market sector is manoeuvring between an escalating legal war of attrition and commercial euphoria.

While state courts pushed their enforcement perimeter beyond retail apps and straight into clearing, platforms continued to print record volume with the CFTC playing the surreal dual role of industry protector and internal prosecutor.

Louisiana Extends Restrictions to Brokers and Clearers

On November 12, a Louisiana court ordered ten prediction-market operators to block users in the state, including Kalshi, Polymarket US and Robinhood. The court order goes beyond the apps: the operators may not broker, clear or settle event contracts for anyone in Louisiana.

Meanwhile, new platforms continue entering the market via partnerships. A Canadian sports prediction-market company, Prospect Markets, launched in the US as an introducing broker on Crypto.com’s infrastructure.

A day earlier, Underdog, which runs its own CFTC-registered exchange, agreed to make its contracts available through Plaee, whose clients will be able to offer those contracts under their own brands without registering as an exchange.

Crypto.com and Underdog are both among the operators named in Louisiana’s order.

The CFTC Is Fighting a Two-Front War

The CFTC continue fighting the states in court. On November 12, the agency and the United States sued Arkansas to stop its case against Kalshi. They argue that the contracts fall under federal derivatives law.

The same agency is also scrutinising Kalshi. Politico and Reuters reported that the CFTC had privately warned Kalshi it could face charges over how it notified the agency of new contracts.

Kalshi told CNBC the issue was a procedural error involving a handful of contracts, many of which were not live.

Kalshi Eyes $65B Valuation Leap

DeFi Rate recorded about $30.4 billion in notional volume across nine venues for November 7–12, with Kalshi accounting for roughly 78% of that volume.

At the same time, the platform is discussing new funding at a $65 billion valuation, a person familiar with the matter told Reuters on November 12. That would be $25 billion more than the $40 billion post-money valuation of its Series G two weeks earlier.

Polymarket reported revenue growth and job cuts in the same week. On November 10, it told CNBC that its annualised revenue had passed $1.8 billion, up from more than $1 billion in June. That figure is the company’s own run rate, not full-year revenue.

The next day, it confirmed that it had cut jobs and ended contractor agreements. It said the reorganisation followed leadership changes and also included new hires.

content:
Bill Miller IV, Chairman and CIO of Miller Value Partners, joins Grace Remington and Sean Hagan on BMTV to explain why he is still bullish on Bitcoin with sentiment near FTX-era lows. He points out that Bitcoin went from 63K to 87K and back to 68K in a matter of months, and argues that volatility is the price of owning great-performing assets. Using the gold analogy, he lays out why Bitcoin’s addressable value is far above its current market cap, and why a supply growing at 80 basis points a year makes it more scarce than gold.

title: OneRoyal Veteran Gebran Massabni Joins PrimaCapital as General Manager
summary:
PrimaCapital has named Gebran Massabni as its new General Manager. He is another former OneRoyal executive joining the management team at the retail FX and CFD broker founded by Ali Marwani. 
Massabni comes to PrimaCapital after spending over 17 years at OneRoyal, where he held several senior roles,...
content:
2026-11-13T21:33:10.816+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 19:33 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Gebran Massabni joins PrimaCapital after more than 17 years at OneRoyal.
  • He reunites with several OneRoyal alumni at PrimaCapital, including founder Ali Marwani.

PrimaCapital has named Gebran Massabni as its new General Manager. He is another former OneRoyal executive joining the management team at the retail FX and CFD broker founded by Ali Marwani.

Massabni comes to PrimaCapital after spending over 17 years at OneRoyal, where he held several senior roles, including Head of Business Development and Chief Operating Officer. In 2023 he was named Head of Global Sales.

Massabni’s new role at PrimaCapital appears in the speaker program for the Forex Traders Expo & Summit Dubai, which takes place later this month. However, PrimaCapital has not shared details about his responsibilities or when he will officially start.

PrimaCapital Builds Team around OneRoyal

Alumni Massabni is joining a company that already has ties to his previous employer. Marwani started PrimaCapital in 2023 after spending ten years at OneRoyal and its predecessor, Royal Financials, which he joined in 2011. Both companies work in the retail trading sector and offer leveraged products like FX and CFDs.

Massabni brings experience from a well-established, multi-licensed broker to a newer company that competes in similar markets, especially in the Middle East.

He is not the only former OneRoyal employee at PrimaCapital. Public records show that Mohammad Jawad Rashid is now Head of Risk at PrimaCapital after previously working as Head of Market Research at OneRoyal.

It is unclear if these hires are part of a planned recruitment strategy.

UAE Activities Run through a Separate Company

According to its website, PrimaCapital’s main operating company is PrimaCapital Limited, which is registered in Saint Lucia under number 2023-00550. The broker provides CFDs through MetaTrader 5.

PrimaCapital’s activities in the UAE are more limited in scope. The company says that all introducing activities in the country are handled only by Prima Global Financials LLC, which holds a Category 5 licence from the UAE Capital Market Authority.

This licence allows for client introductions and promotion, but not full brokerage or execution services in the UAE. This is an important distinction as Massabni steps into his new role as General Manager.

Mark Suman, co-founder and CEO of Maple AI, joins BMTV to talk about private AI built so that even its own team cannot read your chats. He says AI is weaving its way into every aspect of life, including financial transactions and agents paying each other, and he would not want those chats read by a company whose source code you cannot inspect. Maple was built from the ground up with open-source code and encryption. Much like Bitcoin, he wants people not to trust the company, but to verify. All of your data, all of your thoughts, everything that’s precious to you stays encrypted all the way throughout the pipeline, and he says you do not have to sacrifice security to use the best open-weight models.

title: Coincheck Scraps Aplo Brokerage in $18.8M Reversal, Folding Tech into 3iQ
summary:
Coincheck Group is winding down its French institutional crypto prime broker, Aplo, just 13 months after acquisition. 
The group recorded an $18.8 million impairment tied to Aplo for the quarter ended September, contributing to a $26.3 million net quarterly loss, compared with a $2.3 million profit ...
content:
2026-11-13T19:58:47.139+02:00

Friday, 13/11/2026 | 17:58 GMT by Tanya Chepkova

  • Aplo has closed onboarding and entered a phased withdrawal mode through 27 January.
  • Coincheck is repurposing Aplo architecture to power segregated institutional crypto portfolios (SMAs) under its 3iQ subsidiary.

Coincheck Group is winding down its French institutional crypto prime broker, Aplo, just 13 months after acquisition.

The group recorded an $18.8 million impairment tied to Aplo for the quarter ended September, contributing to a $26.3 million net quarterly loss, compared with a $2.3 million profit a year earlier.

The Tokyo-listed crypto fintech giant abandoned the idea to run a standalone European brokerage. Aplo will end its client services by 12 February 2027, and its intellectual property and trading architecture will become a part of a newly created asset-management subsidiary, 3iQ.

A Three-Month Runway to Unwind Balances

Aplo announced the decision to cease operations on 12 November, immediately closing its doors to new accounts and notifying the institutional clients of the termination of their service agreement.

Under the contractual notice period, Aplo has three months to wind down operations and withdraw funds. All accounts will be switched to “withdraw-only” mode no later than 27 January 2027.

Clients can convert holdings into USDC, EURC, or fiat before sweeping funds to external wallets or bank accounts. Any assets remaining by the February cut-off will be liquidated into euros and wired to clients’ registered bank accounts.

Aplo reported no balance-sheet holes or frozen assets, noting that French regulators are notified of the process. Furthermore, Coincheck highlighted Aplo’s MiCA-compliant status, indicating the closure was driven by commercial viability rather than regulatory rejection.

Technology Harvested for 3iQ’s Managed Accounts

Coincheck acquired Aplo in October 2025, when the brokerage served more than 60 active institutional clients, with plans to expand Aplo’s liquidity access, financing products and execution services for banks and institutional investors.

Thirteen months later, management decided that its technology has greater value inside 3iQ than in a small standalone European brokerage.

Approximately half of Aplo’s current employees have been invited to join 3iQ and work on the separately managed account product.

The project will use Aplo’s software and infrastructure to launch managed crypto accounts (SMAs) for institutions and high-net-worth investors in the first half of 2027.

The ultimate test of the retreat now shifts to execution: whether salvaging Aplo’s code for 3iQ can justify the write-down and recoup value from an acquisition that unravelled in barely a year.

title: FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

FutureBit’s Apollo III Bitcoin Miner Hits Micro Center Shelves in Its First Brick-and-Mortar Launch
The Brooklyn company's compact home miner, rated at up to 18 TH/s and starting at $1,099.99, goes on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, including the chain's new Austin locatio...
content:
FutureBit is putting its Apollo III Full Node on sale Friday at four Micro Center stores, the first time customers can walk into a shop and take home one of the Brooklyn company’s bitcoin miners.

The compact home miner, which also runs a full bitcoin node, will be sold in Brooklyn, Miami, Tustin, California, and Austin, Texas, as those stores open Friday, FutureBit said in a release. The four-store launch coincides with the grand opening of Micro Center’s new Austin store, the chain’s 31st U.S. location and its third in Texas.

Customers will also be able to reserve a unit online for in-store pickup, the company said. It did not say how many units each store has in stock, or what Micro Center is charging for them.

Until now, buyers in North America had to order the machine from FutureBit’s website, where the company says units are in stock and ship in two to three days. Putting it on a computer-store shelf lets a customer look at the hardware, ask how it works and carry it out the same day.

“When we started FutureBit, we made weekly trips to the DIY electronics section at the Brooklyn Micro Center to buy parts,” said John Stefanopoulos, founder of FutureBit. “On Friday, someone can walk into that same store, ask how Bitcoin mining works and take home a miner we designed just down the street. We couldn’t be more excited to work with Micro Center on our first physical store launch.”

A 6-inch miner that also runs a full node

FutureBit’s own shop lists the Apollo III Full Node at $1,099.99 without a storage drive, $1,299.99 with 1 terabyte of SSD storage and $1,399.99 with 2 terabytes. A cheaper, miner-only “Standard” model starts at $899.99 but does not include the full node.

The Full Node is rated at up to 18 terahashes per second in Turbo mode, at about 325 watts. In Eco mode, it is listed at about 12 TH/s and 150 watts, with noise under 35 decibels. A Super Eco mode is listed at about 8 TH/s and 80 watts. Power can be adjusted from 50 to 400 watts, and Turbo mode is much louder, at about 55 decibels. Those power figures are measured at the board and can vary by 10%, the product page says.

The unit is a 6.5-by-6.5-by-6-inch cube that weighs 6.5 pounds, comes with a one-year limited warranty and is assembled in the United States. It uses new 3-nanometer, American-designed chips, a custom controller and 8 GB of memory, and it includes a built-in solo mining pool. Buyers can also point the miner at a standard bitcoin mining pool. FutureBit says the full node and solo-mining features require an SSD, which is not included in the $1,099.99 configuration.

Home mining is not a profit play

Bitcoin Magazine covered the Apollo III’s debut in February, when FutureBit introduced the hardware as a way for individuals to run both a miner and a node at home. The point, the company has long argued, is not to compete with industrial mines on cost.

A single Apollo III at 18 TH/s is a sliver of the bitcoin network. A home-scale setup in that range still faces expected times to a solo block measured in centuries at recent difficulty, Bitcoin Magazine previously noted. Even so, a miner running through FutureBit’s Apollo Solo setup found block 973,262 on Oct. 26 and collected the full 3.154 bitcoin reward.

FutureBit, based in Brooklyn, has built consumer mining hardware since 2015. Stefanopoulos has framed store shelves as a way to put more hash rate and more nodes in living rooms. The company did not say whether the Micro Center test will expand beyond the four stores that began selling the Apollo III on Friday.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.

title: Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume Falls 48% in October as Event Contracts More Than Double
Robinhood customers traded $17 billion of crypto in October, down 48% from a year earlier, while event contracts traded jumped 136% to 5.9 billion.
This post Robinhood’s Crypto Trading Volume...
content:
Crypto trading on Robinhood fell by almost half from a year ago in October, the company said Thursday, as customers traded $17 billion of digital assets while their bets on event contracts more than doubled.

The $17 billion figure was down 21% from September and 48% from October 2025, when crypto notional volume reached $32.5 billion. It covers both the flagship Robinhood app and Bitstamp, the crypto exchange the company bought in 2025.

Volume in the Robinhood app fell to $6.8 billion, down 24% from September and 51% from a year earlier. Bitstamp handled $10.2 billion, down 18% month over month and 45% year over year.

Average daily crypto volume across both platforms came to $548 million, compared with $713 million in September and about $1.05 billion a year ago. Daily average crypto trades slipped to about 700,000 from 900,000 in September and 1.1 million in October 2025.

Event contracts take off as crypto cools

The contrast with Robinhood’s prediction markets business is stark. Customers traded 5.9 billion event contracts in October, up 5% from September and 136% from the 2.5 billion traded a year earlier. Average daily volume reached 190 million contracts.

Robinhood counts crypto and prediction markets on the same 31-day calendar, since both trade every day, so the comparison is apples to apples. Event contracts let users bet on outcomes such as elections, sports and economic data, and October’s tally covered the final weeks before the Nov. 3 midterm elections.

That growth has drawn scrutiny in Washington. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is set to chair the Senate Banking Committee in January, plans to crack down on prediction markets and election betting platforms.

The rest of Robinhood’s brokerage held up better than crypto. Equity notional volume rose 2% from a year earlier to $325 billion, and options contracts traded climbed 8% to 289 million. Margin balances reached $22.9 billion, up 39% year over year.

Funded customers rose by about 130,000 in the month to 28.9 million, and net deposits came to $15.1 billion. Total platform assets slipped 3% from September to $383 billion but were up 12% from a year earlier.

Robinhood did not say why crypto activity fell. The release, like all of the company’s monthly updates, is unaudited and preliminary.

Retail pulls back as bitcoin slides

The slump in Robinhood’s crypto numbers lines up with a broader retreat by retail traders. Bitcoin ended September near $83,500 and has slid since, falling below $70,000 early Friday for the first time since August as a hot inflation report raised bets on a Federal Reserve rate hike in December.

Institutional demand has cooled alongside it. U.S. spot bitcoin exchange-traded funds posted a sixth straight day of net outflows on Thursday, and BlackRock’s IBIT, the largest of them, bled about $2 billion over nine sessions through Wednesday. Spot bitcoin ETFs have now erased their net inflows for 2026.

Crypto trading generates transaction revenue for Robinhood, so lower volume generally means fewer fees, even when assets on the platform keep growing. The company reports full fourth-quarter results early next year, and October’s figures are the first look at how the quarter started.

The company has kept expanding its crypto footprint anyway. In October, Robinhood won a license in Dubai to offer bitcoin and stock trading in the Middle East starting in 2027.

Robinhood also said cash and deposit balances fell 20% in October to $16.4 billion, mostly because customers were net buyers, and that the decline has largely reversed in early November. November’s operating data will show whether this month’s selloff below $70,000 brought crypto traders back or pushed more of them toward event contracts.

content:
Mason Lynaugh, executive director of Stand With Crypto, joins BMTV to talk through what the midterms mean for Bitcoin and crypto.

Mason Lynaugh, executive director of Stand With Crypto, joins BMTV to talk through what the midterms mean for Bitcoin and crypto. Stand With Crypto’s race tracker showed 29 of 45 endorsed candidates winning. Mason’s first reason for optimism is the makeup of Congress itself: about 96 pro-crypto members in 2023, and over 300 heading into the 120th, which he calls a pro-crypto majority you could get excited about. The second is that crypto voters made their voices heard in tight races. In Darren Soto’s Florida 9, Soto won by around 1,400 votes in a district with 11,000 Stand With Crypto advocates, and Mason says they genuinely think crypto voters moved that election.

title: President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
summary:
Bitcoin Magazine

President Trump Taps Two Democrats in Bipartisan Slate of SEC and CFTC Nominees as Both Agencies Run Short-Handed
The White House sent four SEC and CFTC nominees to the Senate on Thursday, including former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson and two staffers who worked on the Clarity...
content:
President Donald Trump sent the Senate four nominees for the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission on Thursday, his first picks for either agency in about a year and the first Democrats he has put forward for them.

Former CFTC Commissioner Kristin Johnson, a Democrat, and Republican Steven Levine were nominated to the SEC. Republican Nathan Anonick and Democrat Matthew Rowland were nominated to the CFTC, Bloomberg Law reported.

Each nominee needs Senate confirmation. The Senate Banking Committee will handle the SEC picks, while the Senate Agriculture Committee will take up the CFTC pair before any vote by the full chamber.

Who the nominees are

Levine was tapped for the SEC seat left by Hester Peirce, whose term expired, for a term running through June 5, 2030. He most recently served as general counsel and a senior adviser at the White House Council of Economic Advisers and previously worked at the SEC as counsel and deputy chief of staff to Commissioner Mark Uyeda.

Peirce led the SEC’s Crypto Task Force and was one of the agency’s most vocal supporters of clearer crypto rules.

Johnson would take the seat formerly held by Democrat Caroline Crenshaw, for a term ending June 5, 2029. She served as a CFTC commissioner until 2025 and is a former law school professor. During her time at the CFTC, she spoke often about digital assets, including custody and decentralized finance.

Both CFTC nominees come from the Senate Agriculture Committee, which oversees the derivatives regulator. Anonick is legislative counsel to Chairman John Boozman and was a lead negotiator on the committee’s portion of the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031.

Rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee who also worked on the Clarity Act and the committee’s 2024 crypto bill. He previously served on Johnson’s staff at the CFTC, according to his LinkedIn profile. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028.

Both agencies can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from one party. The SEC currently has two, Chairman Paul Atkins and Commissioner Mark Uyeda. Chairman Mike Selig is the CFTC’s only sitting commissioner.

Lame-duck timing and a Democratic Senate

The timing puts the nominees in front of a Senate in its lame-duck session, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, one of crypto’s sharpest critics, is expected to chair the Banking Committee when the new Congress is seated in January.

The pairing of Democrats with Republicans could matter for confirmation. After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he did not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president filled Democratic seats at agencies such as the SEC, a step he called unlikely. Thursday’s slate does exactly that at both regulators.

The nominations also land with crypto market structure legislation stalled. The Clarity Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it.

Without new law, the SEC and CFTC have set crypto policy largely on their own this year. Selig’s CFTC opened the door to equity perpetual futures, and a federal judge later said the agency likely overstepped while letting trading continue.

The White House did not say when it expects the Senate to act. The open question is whether a Senate heading for Democratic control moves the four nominees before January, or leaves the SEC and CFTC running with skeleton commissions into 2027.

Micah Zimmerman

Micah first discovered Bitcoin in 2018 but remained a skeptic on the sidelines for too long. Since 2021, he has covered crypto and business and now works as a news reporter for Bitcoin Magazine, based in North Carolina.
